Last updated: 30 October 2026
Status: Method 1 used by me a few times; not formally tested. Methods 2 and 3 are compiled research, not yet tried.
Applies to # Written for my setup: a CrossFire PRO with IHS and THC, FireControl’s Straight Cut tool, the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) on 230 V, and the X45 machine torch. The job is a straight cut that has to start right at the edge of a plate, like trimming a sheet or cutting a strip.
Doesn’t cover: Mach3 / Gen1 legacy machines, or programs made in SheetCAM or Fusion. Those use the post’s IHS sequence (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height), not the Straight Cut tool.
I couldn’t find a written Langmuir edge-start procedure for the Straight Cut tool (as of October 2026). Method 1 is the one I use; I’ve used it a few times and it worked, but it isn’t formally tested. Methods 2 and 3 are worked out from forum posts and haven’t been tried. Try every method on scrap first.
What the Straight Cut tool does (per Langmuir staff and support) # From https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/20335:
IHS on (support’s answer, quoted in post #4): “In Straight Cut mode, IHS will automatically set pierce height to 0.15” and THC will automatically set cut height to 0.06". These defaults cannot be changed at this time." IHS off (Langmuir staff, account langmuirsystems, post #5): The tool only does XY moves. The cut height is wherever the Z axis is sitting when you press start. “The no-IHS straight cut program does not have THC enable and disable commands so THC will not activate.” ChelanJim (experienced forum member) agrees, post #10. Other posters in the same thread: toolboy (#3) says with THC on, start with the torch just above the metal edge. ds690 (#2) says the cut height is always 0.06. Newer FireControl versions may behave differently. Check the version you have. Why edge starts fail # IHS on: IHS needs metal under the torch to touch off. Start just off the edge and there’s nothing to touch, so the torch keeps going down or the sequence faults. IHS off: the torch stays at whatever height Z is parked at. That’s usually far too high for the arc to transfer. The Razorcut 45 DI manual (a related but different model; I haven’t found the figure for mine) gives a 3–5 mm transfer distance (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Torch goes out right after the pierce. t/21622 (a CUT45 on a PRO) found three causes: A FireControl bug in 21.1.4, fixed in 21.1.5. Update first. A bad solder joint in the THC cable (FultzForge). Torch lead and work lead crossed or coiled (ds690). Turning THC off made the cut run for several people, but that’s a diagnostic step, not the fix (THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives). Before you start (every method) # FireControl 21.1.5 or newer (t/21622). Z travel check. Lower the torch until the tip just touches the metal. There should still be about 1/2–3/4 in of Z travel left below that (ds690, t/47251). If Z bottoms out first, IHS trips early and the heights are wrong. Raise the torch in the mount. Clean work clamp on the work, and separate the leads: torch lead, work lead, THC cable, and USB not crossed or coiled (Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise). Air 75 psi with the gas test (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables). Amps set on the knob (CUT45 cut settings). Eye protection, ventilation, and fire watch (Langmuir safety page; my CUT45 manual). Method 1: Scrap lead-in piece (Bernie’s method) # Status: used by me a few times; worked; not formally tested. Log each use until there are measured results.
The idea: butt a scrap piece tight against the edge where the cut starts. IHS touches off on the scrap and the arc pierces and gets going there, then carries across the joint into the part.
Pick the scrap. Same thickness as the part. Flat, with a straight, clean edge. Big enough to start the cut about 0.5 in back from the joint, plus room to clamp or weight it. Make a tight butt joint. Push the scrap’s edge hard against the part’s edge where the cut starts. There should be no gap, and the top surfaces should be level, so the torch doesn’t hit a step. Keep both pieces in the work-clamp circuit. The part has the work clamp on clean metal. The scrap sits on the slats and touches the part, so it’s connected too. If you’re not sure, check continuity from the work clamp to the scrap with a meter. Line up the cut. Jog the torch over the scrap, on the cut line, about 0.5 in before the joint. Use the Marker Pen or a pointer to check that the line crosses the joint where you want it. Straight Cut with IHS on. Set the length so it runs from the scrap start point, across the joint, through the part. FireControl sets the 0.15 in pierce and 0.06 in cut height (t/20335 #4). Dry run with the plasma off and watch the path. Cut. Watch the arc cross the joint. Note whether it stutters, the torch moves up or down, or the arc goes out. Log it: thickness, amps, feed, joint gap (none / small), what happened at the joint, and the quality of the edge where the cut entered the part. Why it probably works (reasoning worked out for this page, not from a source): IHS and the pierce both happen on solid metal, and the arc is already cutting at full height and speed when it reaches the part’s edge.
Method 2: start just inside the edge with IHS on (not yet tried) # Not yet tried. It follows from support’s description of IHS-on behavior (t/20335 #4).
Place the start 0.25–0.5 in inside the plate edge, on the cut line, so IHS has metal to touch. Straight Cut, IHS on. FireControl pierces at 0.15 and cuts at 0.06. Trade-off: the pierce leaves a mark in the plate. Use this only if the pierce lands on the scrap side or the first bit can be trimmed off. Log the result as for Method 1. Method 3: IHS off, torch set by hand, start just off the edge (not yet tried) # Not yet tried. It follows from staff’s description of IHS-off behavior (t/20335 #5).
Switch the CUT45 off. Jog the torch over the plate near the edge. Lower Z until a 0.060 in feeler gauge just slides between the shield and the plate. Jog in X/Y only to a start point just off the edge (Z stays put). Switch the CUT45 back on. Run Straight Cut with IHS off. There’s no THC in this mode (staff, t/20335 #5). If the plate isn’t flat, the height drifts. Use it only on short, flat cuts, and weight or clamp the plate flat. Log the result as for Method 1. Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Torch keeps going down off the edge, or IHS faults IHS-on start with no metal under the torch Method 1 or 2 (t/20335 #4) No arc transfer; torch stays high IHS off with Z parked too high Method 3 height set by gauge (t/20335 #5; Razorcut 45 DI manual 3–5 mm transfer) Pierces, then torch goes out FireControl 21.1.4 bug; THC cable joint; crossed leads Update to 21.1.5+; inspect the THC cable; separate leads (t/21622) IHS trips early or heights look wrong Z bottoming out Leave 1/2–3/4 in of Z travel (ds690, t/47251) Arc stutters at the scrap joint (Method 1) Gap at the joint, step in height, or scrap not grounded Tighter butt; same-thickness flat scrap; check continuity to the clamp Height drifts along the cut (Method 3) No THC in IHS-off Straight Cut Flatten the plate; keep the cut short; or use Method 1 Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # Cut height in Straight Cut. Support (t/20335 #4): with IHS on, it’s fixed at 0.06. ds690 (#2): “always 0.06”. Staff (#5): with IHS off, it’s wherever Z sits. These don’t conflict; they describe the two modes. Go with the Langmuir staff and support answers. THC on edge starts. toolboy (#3) talks about THC on with the torch above the edge. Staff (#5) says THC doesn’t activate with IHS off. Go with staff: no THC in IHS-off Straight Cut. Turning THC off to stop torch-out (t/21622). It worked for several people, but the real fixes were the FireControl update and wiring. THC off is a diagnostic step only. Methods 2 and 3 vs. Method 1. I’ve used Method 1 a few times on my machine and it worked. Methods 2 and 3 haven’t been tried yet. Method 1 is my first choice. Safety # Follow Langmuir’s safety page and my CUT45 manual: eye protection to ANSI Z87.1 / Z49.1, ventilation, fire watch. Switch the CUT45 off before putting a gauge or hands under the torch. Plate and scrap edges are sharp; wear gloves.
Sources # Forum, Straight Cut behavior: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/20335 (#2 ds690; #3 toolboy; #4 support quote; #5 Langmuir staff langmuirsystems; #10 ChelanJim) Forum, torch out after pierce: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/21622 (FireControl 21.1.4 → 21.1.5; FultzForge THC cable; ds690 leads; THC-off reports) Forum, Z travel: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/47251 (ds690) Langmuir, FireControl guide: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol-guide Langmuir, THC guide: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/thc-guide Langmuir, Safety: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/safety Razorweld Razorcut 45 DI manual 2022 (a related but different model, not my JRWPC45LH) (transfer distance; safety): https://razorweld.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/RAZORCUT45DI-INSTRUCTION-MANUAL-2022.pdf Bernie’s own shop experience (Method 1, used a few times; no measurements recorded). Bernie’s test results # Date Method Material / thickness Amps Feed (ipm) FireControl version Joint gap (Method 1) Arc start OK? Crossed joint / edge clean? Notes Not recorded 1 Not recorded Not recorded Not recorded Not recorded Not recorded Worked Not recorded Used a few times; worked; no measurements or dates recorded. Methods 2 and 3: no results yet (as of 30 October 2026).
summary: Three ways to start a FireControl Straight Cut right at the plate edge with IHS on a CrossFire PRO. Method 1, a scrap lead-in piece, is the one I’ve used.

Last updated: 30 October 2026
Status: compiled research, not yet tried. The steps and fixes below are collected from Langmuir documents and forum posts.
Applies to # This covers my CrossFire PRO with the Langmuir LS-THC added on (it’s a $400 option on the PRO), IHS standard, FireControl, and a Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) bought from Langmuir (Langmuir lists it as the “Razorweld Razorcut 45 with Machine Torch”). It uses the plug-and-play 50:1 divider port and the X45 machine torch, on 230 V. Some of the Langmuir docs don’t apply to this setup:
The raw-voltage pigtail wiring in the THC guide is only for cutters without a divider port. The CUT45 has one, so leave the raw wiring alone. The XR ships with THC and has its own wiring and ground notes. The Gen1/Mach3 THC kit is a different system. Powermax arc-voltage tables are for Hypertherm, not the CUT45. Wiring check (do once, and again after any rewiring) # Power everything off. Connect the CUT45’s 2-pin divider port to the VIM DIV INPUT through the Divided Voltage pigtail. Run the VIM output cable to the electronics box. Use DIV OUTPUT, not PV OUTPUT. Polarity: the red wire goes to the negative pin (torch) and the black wire to the positive pin (work clamp). The THC only reads positive voltage. Crossed wires read 0 V. Port-swap check (some units shipped with the ports swapped): with Manual Torch Fire in FireControl, check that the torch fires from the firing port. Then check the other port gives THC voltage. Set up as if ready to cut: THC, IHS, and USB connected, cutter on, work clamp attached (see Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise). Click the red TEST button (THC Health Check) on the FireControl THC panel. Resting voltage (not firing): under 5 V passes. 5–10 V “should still function”. Non-zero live volts with the torch off usually means water bridging the IHS brass contact. See the table below. Make a straight cut with Straight Cut (Zero All Axes first) with the THC panel toggled off, and watch Live Volts. Typical arc voltage is 60–150 V. On the 50:1 port that’s about +1.2 to 3 V. The flowchart treats 85–230 V as in range. 230–280 V is “higher than expected”. Over 280 V can damage the THC. Under 85 V sends you to the isolation/ground checks in Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise. For reference, Razorweld’s rated output voltage is about 96–98 V (96 V in JRWPC45LH dealer listings and the JRWPC45LT manual (the sister model: same CUT45 machine, sold with a different torch); 98 V on Razorweld’s CUT45 spec sheet). That’s a nameplate rating, not a THC setpoint. Settings: start at the Langmuir defaults # Setting Range Default (start here) Nominal Voltage 1–300 V 0 = SMART voltage Voltage Tolerance 0.1–10 V 1.5 V Voltage Sample Size 10–300 50 SMART Voltage Offset 0.01–1 in 0.25 in SMART Voltage Distance 0.01–10 in 0.25 in Torch Speed CUTOFF 1–100 % 85 % Z-Speed Factor 1–99 % 5 % (corrects up to 4 in out of flat over 48 in) What these mean:
SMART voltage reads the arc right after IHS and holds that voltage for the rest of the loop. It resets every loop. With the default offset and distance, THC only engages on loops longer than 0.5 in. Small holes are left alone. THC moves don’t show on the Z DRO. The Z axis is open-loop. Steps: setting a manual nominal voltage (optional) # Use this only if SMART voltage isn’t giving good edges.
Pick the amps and feed rate from your cut settings (CUT45 cut settings). Jog the torch down to the real cut height by hand. The THC guide says a typical gap is 0.060 in; set it with a feeler gauge or shim. Don’t use the SheetCAM 0.08 in value here. That number includes IHS springback, and there’s no IHS in this test (see Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Turn off the electronics box and unplug the Z motor, then power back up. The line test can’t include an IHS loop, or FireControl will alarm. Cut an 8–10 in straight line and read Live Volts. Enter that number as the Nominal Voltage. Plug the Z motor back in. Log it in thc_voltage in the test-cut log, for that material, thickness, amps, and speed. Steps: stopping dives into corners, holes, and the end of a cut # No lead-outs on THC toolpaths. Langmuir’s Fusion guide: “use NO lead out to avoid losing arc voltage at the end of a cut.” The same reasoning applies to SheetCAM. No self-intersecting lead-ins or lead-outs, and don’t cross a cut you’ve already made (THC guide, lost arc). Leave Torch Speed CUTOFF at 85 % or raise it if the torch dives in corners. Below that percentage of program speed, the THC freezes Z. Program speed is the fastest non-lead-in feed in the file. The SheetCAM v1.6 post writes it as (PS…) at the end. So if you cut small holes in a slower operation in the same file, they automatically run with the THC frozen once they’re below 85 % of the fastest feed. (This is from reading the v1.6 post file. Greg9504 says the same: THC off below 85 % speed, thread 8193.) Lower the Z-Speed Factor if it still dives. Default is 5 %. Intricate art that never reaches full speed: the THC never switches on. Either lower the CUTOFF % or program a slower feed (THC guide). Thin sheet that lifts or warps: THC is what keeps height on warped sheet (Langmuir consumables page). Parts under about 15 x 15 in may not need THC at all (PRO FAQ). Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Torch bobs up and down THC over-hunting Raise Sample Size, raise Tolerance, lower Z-Speed Factor (THC guide). Torch plunges into the plate at corners or small holes Arc voltage rises when slowing down Raise Torch Speed CUTOFF %, lower Z-Speed Factor (THC guide). No lead-out. Torch dips at the end of the cut Lead-out losing the arc Remove the lead-out (Fusion guide). THC never turns on Loop under 0.5 in, speed never reaches the CUTOFF, or Tolerance too wide Lower CUTOFF %, check SMART offset + distance, narrow Tolerance (THC guide). Live Volts reads 0.0 V Computer or monitor frame touching the table frame (shields tied together) Separate the frames; check USB shield-to-frame resistance (Holla2040, t/31460/1; Langmuir flowchart). Torch goes out right after the pierce FireControl 21.1.4 bug; bad THC cable joint; crossed or coiled leads; water in the torch Update FireControl; inspect the THC cable; separate leads; dry the air (t/21622). Odd rising or dipping now and then; non-zero Live Volts with the torch off Water or conductive water-table chemistry bridging the IHS brass contact to the lead screw Blow the contact dry and apply dielectric grease (PRO assembly, Z/IHS table; flowchart FLAG 1). Live voltage low (under 85 V) Enclosure not isolated, laptop charger ground, external monitor/desktop Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise isolation steps; laptop on battery; UPS or USB isolator (flowchart). Live Volts 0 Polarity crossed, or wrong port Wiring check steps 2–3. Erratic live voltage on a budget cutter Noisy arc signal Raise Sample Size slowly (THC guide). Arc lost right after the pierce on thin sheet Pierce delay too long Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height. False “arc lost” pause at the start Pierce delay shorter than the cutter’s pilot delay Lengthen the pierce delay (THC guide; Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Torch touches the plate mid-cut IHS switch opens The machine auto-lifts 1/16 in (PRO assembly). Find out why: tipped part, warped sheet, Z-Speed too low. What experienced forum members add # Sources are weighted as described in About this site: Langmuir first, then Razorweld/Jasic, then experienced forum members. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the CUT45.
How SMART picks its voltage. 72Pony (PrimeWeld CUT60, but this is about FireControl, not the cutter), t/27956/23 and t/21289/10. The THC samples the arc voltage in the first few seconds after IHS sets the height, then holds that voltage. So SMART is only as good as the height at the start of the cut. If IHS leaves the torch too high, SMART locks onto the too-high height. Check the real height by pausing a cut (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Voltage goes up as the torch goes up. Cletus, t/14406/2. This matches the THC guide: the THC lowers Z when the voltage reads high. Live Volts reads 0.0 V. Holla2040 (CrossFire PRO with a CUT45, the same cutter as mine), t/31460/1. The cause was a computer monitor frame touching the machine frame. The HDMI shield then tied into the USB shield. His fix: a mini PC on an ungrounded wall-wart power supply. Use one that’s built that way; don’t cut off a ground pin. Check with a meter: resistance from the USB shield to the table frame, as in the Langmuir flowchart (Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise). Torch goes out right after the pierce, sometimes with “TORCH MOVING BEFORE CUTTING VOLTAGE SENSED”. This was thread t/21622, on a CUT45 with a PRO. Causes found there: A FireControl bug in 21.1.4, fixed in 21.1.5. Update FireControl first. Turning THC off made the cut run (ds690, nicaDd, TinWhisperer, toolboy). That’s a way to diagnose, not a fix. A bad solder joint in the THC cable (FultzForge). Torch lead and work lead crossed or coiled (ds690). Water in the torch (jnc5908404). See Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables. nicaDd: plunge rate at least 50 ipm. Commissioning order. TomWS, t/24586/2: Cut a 2 in square. Do an IHS dry run with the plasma off. Cut with THC off. Then cut with THC on. Measure the part and adjust kerf. ChelanJim’s checklist (Hypertherm 45XP), t/41575/4: 6 CFM at 90 psi, and dry. Work lead on clean metal. Torch cable, work lead, THC cable, and USB not touching, crossed, or coiled. Test with a 2 in box with a 3/4 in circle inside. Ferrites. Cletus, t/17886/36: no ferrite on the raw arc-voltage line into his THC. This setup uses the divider port, not raw voltage, so it mostly doesn’t apply. Staff’s advice is chokes on USB (Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise). These don’t conflict. Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # THC off as a fix. Several posters in t/21622 got cuts to run by turning THC off. That hides the problem; it doesn’t fix it. Go with Langmuir’s fix (update FireControl) and the wiring checks. THC off is only a diagnostic step. Normal arc-voltage range. The THC guide says 90–150 V when cutting (raw wiring). The flowchart and PRO troubleshooting say 60–150 V typical, and the flowchart uses 85–230 V as “in range”. Starting choice: the flowchart and troubleshooting numbers. They’re newer (Rev B 2021, troubleshooting updated Dec 2024) and written for the divider port, which this setup uses. THC REF to GND. The flowchart says 3.9–4.3 V DC; PRO troubleshooting says “around 4.0–4.2 V”. Both are Langmuir. Treat 4.0–4.2 V as normal. A reading of 3.9 or 4.3 is borderline: note it and ask Langmuir support. Typical CUT45 cutting voltage. There’s no official value. One community post (thread 38627, an XR owner, general forum member) reports 115–128 V. Langmuir staff in thread 5883 recommend SMART voltage. Starting choice: SMART voltage plus a line test on your own machine (planned here as the test-cut program’s V1 and H1 steps) over any posted number. Lead-out. Langmuir only says “no lead-out” in the Fusion guide. The SheetCAM guide doesn’t say it. The reason (losing arc voltage at the end) is the same with either CAM, so it’s followed in SheetCAM too. Safety # The VIM’s maximum input is 300 V. The Razorcut 45 DI manual (a related but different model) lists a 300 V no-load voltage; I haven’t checked the JRWPC45LH figure in my manual yet, so treat the cutter’s open-circuit voltage as at least that. Never connect raw arc voltage on this setup. The divider port is the factory method. Any wiring inside the plasma cutter is for a qualified person only (Langmuir THC guide; the Razorweld manuals say repairs are for qualified technicians only). Follow the Langmuir safety page: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/safety
Sources # Langmuir, LS-THC guide: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/thc-guide Langmuir, THC troubleshooting flowchart, Rev B 6/16/2021: https://assets.langmuirsystems.com/file/THC+TROUBLESHOOTING+FLOW+CHART.pdf Langmuir, PRO troubleshooting: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/protroubleshooting Langmuir, PRO assembly (Z-Axis & IHS table, 1/16 in auto-lift): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/pro-assembly Langmuir, Fusion guide (“use NO lead out”): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/software-fusion Langmuir, CrossFire PRO FAQ (when THC is needed): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-pro Langmuir, consumables and cut-problem table: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-parts-consumables Langmuir, SheetCAM post v1.6 (program speed logic): https://assets.langmuirsystems.com/firecontrol/posts/FireControl-v1.6.scpost Razorweld Razorcut 45 DI manual 2022 (a related but different model, not my JRWPC45LH) (spec table): https://razorweld.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/RAZORCUT45DI-INSTRUCTION-MANUAL-2022.pdf Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/8193 (langmuir-mike troubleshooting guide; Greg9504), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/5883 (staff: FireControl doesn’t set amps; SMART voltage), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12670 (IHS on, FireControl/post v1.6, laptop on battery), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/38627 (XR, community voltages) Forum, experienced members: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/27956 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/21289 (72Pony: THC sampling), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/14406 (Cletus: voltage vs. height), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31460 (Holla2040: 0.0 V from monitor frame), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/21622 (torch out after pierce; FC 21.1.5), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/24586 (TomWS: commissioning), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/41575 (ChelanJim checklist), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/17886 (Cletus: ferrites), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/35204 (langmuir-mike: THC troubleshooting) Bernie’s test results # No results logged yet (as of 30 October 2026). Results will come from the test-cut log and be listed here with: Date; Material / thickness; Amps; Feed (ipm); SMART V read; Manual nominal V; CUTOFF %; Z-Speed %; Dive?; Notes.
summary: Wiring check, Langmuir default settings, and fixes for torch dives with the Langmuir THC on a CrossFire PRO and a CUT45 using the 50:1 divider port.

Last updated: 30 October 2026
Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads.
Applies to # Any Windows computer that runs FireControl for a CrossFire table. The error comes from the computer, not the table, so the CrossFire model doesn’t matter. Reports in the threads below are from the original CrossFire, the PRO and the XR.
Versions: reported on 21.1.4 and 21.1.5. Langmuir staff say 24.1.6 should fix it (t/26056/67), and the 24.1.6 release notes list “fixes for low power CPU’s which was causing Child Process errors” (t/41980/1). The downloads page lists 24.1.6 as the current Windows version and 21.1.5 as the current Mac version (checked 2026-10-28). Mac: none of the threads read for this page report this error on a Mac. Symptom (what you’ll see) # FireControl crashes on startup, and Windows shows a dialog saying “Child process exited with code 1”. It often starts right after a Windows update. Sometimes it appears after loading a file, or with two FireControl windows open. On the compatibility build, FireControl may open but show no toolpath picture. Likely causes # From langmuir-reilly’s PSA (t/31326/1) and the PRO troubleshooting page, most likely first:
A power-efficient CPU plus a Windows power change. A “child process” is a part of FireControl that runs on its own. Staff name the digital read-out (DRO) and the toolpath visualizer. When one fails, Windows shows “Child process exited with code 1”. Staff link it to a Windows update from around October 2022 that “changed how the operating system distributes power”. After it, some power-efficient CPUs no longer give FireControl enough resources. Most reports are AMD Ryzen processors whose model numbers end in “-U”. A few are AMD “-H” chips. Under 1 % come from Intel computers (t/31326/20). langmuir-zachary (2025, t/26056/67): “it’s mostly caused by the visualizer crashing”. Two copies of FireControl running. Langmuir-Nick has seen the error “just from having two instances of the same program running” (t/31326/30). A corrupt post processor, if the error comes up after loading a file (Bigdaddy2166, t/26056/53). Hardware or an OS the program can’t live with, if it still crashes after every fix below (PRO troubleshooting). Find your CPU model: in Windows 10 or 11, Settings > System > About, under “Device specifications” > “Processor” (t/31326/1). A model ending in U (or an AMD H) matches the pattern.
Fixes (most to least likely) # Before you reinstall anything, back up:
The clean reinstall (fix 4) deletes the .FireControl folder. Langmuir says it holds preferences, soft limits and program history. Write down your Machine Settings and THC settings first. Copy your SheetCAM tool library somewhere safe. One user wiped a computer and lost his (JapScrap, t/26056/27). Work down the list and stop when FireControl opens.
Install the current Windows FireControl (24.1.6) from https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/downloads. This is the staff fix as of 2025 (t/26056/67). Kwikfab fixed his the same way (t/26056/66). Close every copy of FireControl (check Task Manager), then reopen one (t/31326/30). Laptop on wall power: set the power slider to “Best performance”. In 2022, langmuir-reilly asked a user where his battery slider was set and whether “Best Performance” helped (t/26056/9). He didn’t say it was a fix. It’s a quick check. Then restart Windows and open FireControl before opening anything else. Clean reinstall (PRO troubleshooting page, “FireControl Reinstallation”): Uninstall FireControl from the Control Panel. Delete the folder C:\Users\[YOUR USERNAME]\.FireControl. Restart the computer. Reinstall FireControl. Try the compatibility build. Download “FireControl 21.1.5-compatibility” (“for older graphics hardware”) and install it the same clean way. The PRO troubleshooting page lists this step. PatriotPits fixed it this way (t/26056/29). So did Burnswelding (#41) and Bradw_00 (#49). It didn’t work for everyone. geaarogers (#30) and Rodent (#55) still got the crash on the compatibility build. langmuir-zachary still offers it as the fallback in 2025 (t/26056/67). The compatibility version may turn the toolpath visualizer off to save resources. Langmuir: “This is a feature, not a bug!” Turn it back on from the View tab, top left. If the error comes up after loading a file: reload the post processor in case it’s corrupt (Bigdaddy2166, t/26056/53). Only if nothing else works: update the CPU drivers or the BIOS. Staff call these “relatively drastic steps” (t/26056/7). Follow the computer maker’s instructions. Last resort: use a different computer. The troubleshooting page says this may be necessary. Bigdaddy2166 runs three Intel mini PCs that “work perfectly” (t/31326/11, t/31326/32). ChelanJim uses a mini PC at his table (t/31326/26). Langmuir doesn’t recommend specific products (t/31326/20). Quick lookup # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) “Child process exited with code 1” at startup Power-efficient CPU plus the Windows power change; the visualizer crashes Fixes 1–5 (t/31326/1; t/26056/67) Started right after a Windows update Same Same; then pause auto-updates (t/31326/1) Opens on the compatibility build, but there’s no toolpath picture The compatibility build turns the visualizer off View tab > turn the visualizer on (PRO troubleshooting) Error appears with two FireControl windows open Two copies running Close both, then reopen one (t/31326/30) Still crashes after fixes 1–7 Hardware or OS the program can’t live with Different computer (PRO troubleshooting) Keeping it from coming back # On a “U” CPU, staff advise turning off automatic Windows updates. Staff warn that “disabling Windows updates may cause you to miss out on important security updates” (t/31326/1). Turning updates off now won’t fix a computer that already has the update (t/31339/6). Don’t let Windows update while you cut. jamesdhatch (t/26056/45) and ChelanJim (t/26056/43) both say this. Keep a copy of the working installer, and write down which version works. Where sources disagree # Is it Windows or FireControl? In 2023, staff said “this issue stems from Windows, not a problem with the FireControl software” (t/31326/1, t/31339/6). In 2025, staff said 24.1.6 “should fix the issue” (t/26056/67), and the 24.1.6 release notes say the same (t/41980/1). Both are staff. The newer advice comes first here: update first. The older PSA steps are the fallback. Rolling back to 20.6.2. Some users got running again on 20.6.2 (JapScrap, t/26056/27). Phillipw says it works “as long as you are not running a xr or a pro with limit switches” (t/26056/26). Phillipw also reports that another user couldn’t get 20.6 to install on Windows 11 (t/28310/22). It isn’t a Langmuir recommendation, so it’s not in the fix list; it ranks behind the compatibility build. Downgrading Java (jsvalentin, t/26056/61). He made three changes at once: older Java, a new AMD graphics driver, and the compatibility build. There’s only one report, and an old Java build is a security risk, so it’s not in the fix list. The compatibility build is the part that matches the staff advice. Bigdaddy2166’s USB-voltage explanation (t/26056/65): a power-saving AMD chip “tries to regulate the USB voltage”. Staff point to the visualizer instead (t/26056/67). Staff’s explanation of the cause is used here. His practical advice (use a non-power-saving CPU) agrees with staff anyway. Downloading with Chrome instead of Edge (Bently69, t/26056/68). One report, no explanation. Listed only as something to try. What experienced forum members add # Bigdaddy2166, t/26056/53: if the error comes up after loading a file, reload the post processor in case it’s corrupt. ChelanJim, t/26056/57: if FireControl asks to “update” the motion-control firmware from v1.3 to v1.2, let it. It should then offer v1.3; take that too. Turn the control box off and on if needed. He calls this a workaround Langmuir’s techs found. It’s not in the official docs. TomWS, t/31339/2: points new reports to the staff PSA. Safety # Do these fixes with the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) switched off and nothing running on the table. If a reinstall resets your settings, check soft limits and THC settings before the next cut. A table running without its usual limits can crash the gantry.
Sources # Forum, crash on startup: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/26056 (6,229 views, 67 posts; langmuir-reilly #7, #9; Phillipw #26; JapScrap #27; PatriotPits #29; ChelanJim #43, #57; jamesdhatch #45; Bigdaddy2166 #53, #65; jsvalentin #61; Kwikfab #66; langmuir-zachary #67; Bently69 #68; compatibility-build reports #30, #41, #49, #55) Forum, staff PSA: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31326 (langmuir-reilly #1, #6, #20; TomWS #10; Bigdaddy2166 #11, #25, #32; ChelanJim #26; Langmuir-Nick #30) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31339 (langmuir-reilly #6; TomWS #2) Forum, 24.1.6 beta notes: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/41980/1 (langmuir-zachary) Forum, 20.6 on Windows 11: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/28310/22 (Phillipw) Langmuir, PRO troubleshooting (Child Process Error; FireControl Reinstallation; compatibility version): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/protroubleshooting Langmuir, downloads (current versions; 21.1.5-compatibility): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/downloads
summary: FireControl crashes on startup, or Windows shows “Child process exited with code 1”. The most-viewed FireControl problem on the forum. Langmuir staff tie it to power-efficient AMD “U” CPUs and a Windows update; FireControl 24.1.6 is the staff fix.

Last updated: 30 October 2026
Status: compiled research, not yet tried. The clamp location below is my starting choice; the isolation test and fixes come from Langmuir documents and forum posts.
Applies to # Bernie’s setup:
CrossFire PRO with THC and IHS, in a home shop. The electronics enclosure is wall-mounted on plywood away from the table: not touching any metal, and joined to the table only by the motor cables. It sits on one side of the compressor, with the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) on the other side. That gives the frame isolation Langmuir’s isolator mount is there for. Because the box isn’t on the leg, if the flowchart’s isolation test ever reads low, check the motor cable shields and connectors instead of the leg mount. FireControl runs on a computer next to the table. The CUT45 is on a 230 V circuit (JRWPC45LH dealer listings and the JRWPC45LT manual (the sister model: same CUT45 machine, sold with a different torch) give 230 V single-phase ±15 %; the 95–265 V range quoted here before was from the dual-voltage Razorcut 45 DI manual, a different model). The table electronics run on a separate 120 V, 20 A outlet. Doesn’t cover:
The XR’s grounding instructions (clamp straight to the workpiece) are for a different machine. The Mach3/Gen1 legacy noise fixes are for old electronics. Hypertherm’s HF-start notes don’t apply. The CUT45 uses a non-high-frequency (NHF) pilot start. Safety first: defer to the manufacturers # House wiring, the 230 V receptacle, and grounding the supply are an electrician’s job. Langmuir: wire to the National Electrical Code and hire a licensed electrician. The Razorcut 45 DI manual (a related but different model) says connections only by a qualified person, ground the power supply well, and power extension leads are not recommended for inverter cutters. The JRWPC45LT manual (the sister model: same CUT45 machine, sold with a different torch) points to ANSI Z49.1 for electrical safety and recommends an RCD safety switch. If you have to run long torch or work leads, use a larger cable size. Residential supply: an earlier version of this page quoted an EMC Class A, “not to be connected to a residential low-voltage power supply grid” warning. That came from the Razorcut 45 DI manual, a different model. The safety section of my own JRWPC45LH manual has no such wording, so I’ve removed it. Follow your own cutter’s manual and Langmuir’s safety page, and have a licensed electrician handle the 230 V circuit. Never defeat or remove a safety ground on the cutter, the table, or the house wiring. The power supply switch on the table electronics must match the wall outlet the electronics plug into (120 V), not the plasma cutter’s voltage (Langmuir PRO page). Make every connection with the power off. The Razorcut 45 DI manual (related model) warns that high voltage stays inside after switch-off; treat the CUT45 the same way. Links: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/safety, my printed JRWPC45LH manual, and (related model only) the Razorcut 45 DI manual (§5, Installation).
Steps: work clamp and grounding # Clean the clamp spot to bare metal. Langmuir: “poor clamp contact on clean metal” is a cause of the arc not transferring. The Razorcut 45 DI manual’s error table (related model) also lists checking the earth clamp when the cutting circuit is blocked. Clamp location (see the conflict below). My starting choice is the water-table drain plug, as the FireControl guide and the CrossFire assembly guide say. Follow the THC flowchart’s tests using the slat bed as the flowchart says. Check that the clamp spot, slats, and workpiece are all connected. Set a multimeter to resistance (or continuity). Probe from the clamp spot to a slat, then to the top of the workpiece. If you don’t get continuity to the workpiece (rust, mill scale, paint under the sheet), clamp to the workpiece directly for that job. Keep the clamp lead and the torch lead apart from the USB cable and the motor cables wherever you can. This isn’t stated as a step in the official docs checked for this page; it follows from the general reason Langmuir gives for EMI (see the forum sources) and costs nothing to do. Steps: isolating the electronics (from the Langmuir THC flowchart) # Do these with everything set up as for cutting: THC, IHS, and USB connected, computer on, cutter on, work clamp on.
Resistance test. Set the meter to resistance. Probe the silver shell of the USB plug where it enters the electronics box, then the slat bed where the work clamp is connected. Langmuir’s pass value is more than 10,000 ohms. If it’s under 10,000 ohms, unplug the USB cable from the electronics box, take the work clamp off the slat bed, and measure again. Still low: the enclosure is touching the frame. Take the box off the leg (3 screws) and try a cut. (My box is already off the table on the wall, so on my setup this step means checking that nothing metal touches it.) It has to sit on the boomerang-shaped plastic isolator mount, and the mounting screws mustn’t dig into the box’s sheet metal. If you never got the isolator, contact Langmuir support (support@langmuirsystems.com, per the flowchart). OK with the USB unplugged: the problem is the computer’s ground. Laptop: unplug the charger and run on battery. If the laptop sits on a metal stand that touches the frame, put cardboard between laptop and stand. Repeat the live-voltage test. Desktop PC or external monitor: run them on a UPS, or power the electronics through a USB voltage isolator (Langmuir sells one). Motor and IHS plugs: check that the D-sub motor plugs are screwed in and not arc-damaged (PRO assembly troubleshooting). Keep the IHS contact dry; water-table water bridging the brass contact gives false voltage (THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives). Re-run the THC TEST (Health Check) and a straight-line cut and confirm normal Live Volts (THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives). Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Arc won’t transfer; pilot arc only Poor clamp contact, worn electrode, loose consumables Clean bare-metal clamp spot; check consumables (Langmuir consumables page). Low live voltage (under about 85 V) Enclosure touching the frame; computer ground through the charger or monitor Isolation steps 1–4 (flowchart). Non-zero voltage with the torch off; random THC moves Moisture or water-table chemistry at the IHS brass contact Blow dry, apply dielectric grease, re-test (flowchart FLAG 1; PRO assembly). FireControl disconnects, or motion freezes when the arc starts Electrical noise into USB Laptop on battery; UPS or USB isolator; route cables apart; then see the staff fix below. Motor skips only while cutting Noise or arc damage at the motor plugs Check and screw in the D-sub plugs (PRO assembly troubleshooting). If noise problems persist # These are not first steps. Do them only after the steps above, ideally after talking to Langmuir support.
Ferrite chokes on cables / a board-level inductor fix. Posted by Langmuir staff (langmuir-daniel) in thread 9175. The board version it was written for isn’t confirmed. Ask Langmuir whether it applies to your PRO’s board before soldering anything. An isolated 0–5 V signal converter. A community fix from Kytor (thread 39578, long-time forum member). It’s a modification, so don’t do it unless support agrees. A dedicated earth ground rod for the table. One community post (thread 38627, an XR owner, general forum member) gives a resistance target. Don’t take an earthing number from a forum post. Grounding rods and bonding are for a licensed electrician. What experienced forum members add # Sources are weighted as described in About this site: Langmuir first, then Razorweld/Jasic, then experienced forum members. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the CUT45.
Never remove or defeat a safety ground. Some forum members posted that they removed the ground pin on a PC or monitor, or used a 2-prong “cheater” adapter. Don’t do that. This page doesn’t recommend it. Follow the manufacturers’ grounding instructions and a licensed electrician; experienced members TomWS and Bigdaddy2166 also warn against it (t/24659/16). To break a ground loop, run the laptop on battery, or use a USB ground-loop isolator or a UPS.
Why isolation matters. TomWS, t/35669/19. The work clamp is both the plasma’s current return and the THC’s voltage reference. The table touches it all the time through the slats. So keep the control electronics isolated from the table, and tie together only the grounds that need to be tied, at one point (a “star” ground). He built this into his own enclosure. On the PRO, Langmuir’s design already does the job (the control box’s isolation and the flowchart’s >10,000 ohm test), so follow Langmuir’s steps and take TomWS’s idea as the reason why. **Don’t float the whole system. TomWS and Bigdaddy2166 **, t/24659/16: removing the safety ground from the whole system is “craziness”. Ground loops between the computer and the control box. Bigdaddy2166 (Everlast cutter), t/32012/17 and t/36138/1. A computer and a control box on the same building ground can make a loop. Use an ohm test to find it. His fix: a USB ground-loop isolator. That’s the recommended fix here too. He also suggested a non-grounding plug adapter on the control box. Don’t do that part; it defeats the safety ground. EMI ground straps on the motors (t/48104/10) are a later step if noise persists. Cletus (PrimeWeld CUT60), t/17886/36 and t/9175/136. He has the control box isolated, and a 15 ft USB cable with ferrites on both ends. He found his interference was a ground loop. He also removed PC and monitor ground pins. Don’t copy that; never remove ground pins. Monitor frame touching the table. Holla2040 (same CUT45), t/31460/1. The THC read 0.0 V until he separated the frame. His fix was a mini PC on a factory-ungrounded wall wart. Keep computer and monitor frames off the table and gantry. 72Pony, t/24052/24: ferrite chokes on the USB. He also suggested an ungrounded plug. Don’t do that part; it defeats the safety ground. Cable routing and clamping. ChelanJim, t/41575/4: work lead on clean metal. Torch cable, work lead, THC cable, and USB must not touch, cross, or coil. Wsidr1, t/35218/5: clamp onto the part at the start of every cut, and uncoil power cords. Bigdaddy2166, t/43254/14, and nicaDd (long-time forum member), t/45396/3: clamp on the metal being cut, not on the slats. ds690, t/21622: crossed or coiled leads caused torch-out problems. Magnetic clamps on aluminum or stainless. jamesdhatch (long-time forum member), t/31161/8: put a steel strip under the sheet so the magnet clamp has something to grab and the circuit still goes through the work. Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # Safety ground (some forum members remove the PC ground pin or use a 2-prong adapter). Cletus, 72Pony, and Bigdaddy2166 (in one post) suggested it. TomWS and Bigdaddy2166 (t/24659/16) call floating the safety ground “craziness”. Never remove or defeat a safety ground. Follow the manufacturers’ grounding instructions and a licensed electrician (TomWS and Bigdaddy2166 agree). To break a ground loop, use a laptop on battery, a USB ground-loop isolator, or a UPS instead.
Clamp on the part vs. the drain plug. Several experienced members (Wsidr1, Bigdaddy2166, ChelanJim, nicaDd) clamp on the workpiece itself, on clean metal. That agrees with the Razorcut 45 DI manual’s general advice to clamp close to the cut. Suggested: clamp on the part when you can, and always on clean metal.
Where the work clamp goes (Langmuir documents give different clamp locations).
THC guide (2020): machine frame. FireControl guide and CrossFire assembly: water-table drain plug. THC flowchart Rev B (2021): slat bed (one step also says “machine frame”). XR guide: straight to the workpiece. Community (thread 12670): ground to the material. Bernie’s starting choice: the drain plug by default (the PRO-era operating guide), the slat bed for the flowchart tests, and the workpiece as a test whenever transfer or cut quality is poor. Not yet confirmed: whether the slats and drain plug are bonded to the frame. It’s on my list to ask Langmuir support: “On a CrossFire PRO with the stainless water table, which clamp point do you recommend now, and are the slats and drain plug bonded to the frame?”
Ground-rod resistance target. That’s community (XR) only. Defer to a licensed electrician and the NEC.
Sources # Langmuir, Safety (NEC, electrician): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/safety Langmuir, THC troubleshooting flowchart Rev B: https://assets.langmuirsystems.com/file/THC+TROUBLESHOOTING+FLOW+CHART.pdf Langmuir, THC guide (clamp on frame; wiring): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/thc-guide Langmuir, FireControl guide (clamp on drain plug): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol-guide Langmuir, CrossFire assembly (clamp on drain plug): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-assembly Langmuir, XR assembly (clamp on workpiece; XR only): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/xr-assembly Langmuir, PRO troubleshooting: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/protroubleshooting Langmuir, PRO assembly (motor plugs, IHS contact): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/pro-assembly Langmuir, CrossFire PRO page (power supply switch matches the outlet): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-pro Langmuir, consumables and cut problems: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-parts-consumables Razorweld Razorcut 45 DI manual 2022 (a related but different model, not my JRWPC45LH) (§5 Installation; extension leads; earth clamp. Its Class A EMC / residential-supply warning isn’t in my JRWPC45LH manual and is no longer used here): https://razorweld.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/RAZORCUT45DI-INSTRUCTION-MANUAL-2022.pdf Langmuir, “Razorweld Razorcut 45 with Machine Torch” product page (NHF start): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/products/razorweld-razorcut-45-with-machine-torch Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/9175 (langmuir-daniel, chokes/inductor fix), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/39578 (Kytor, isolated converter), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31057 (laptop on battery), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12670 (ground to material), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/38627 (XR grounding, community) Forum, experienced members: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/35669 (TomWS: isolation, star ground), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/24659 (TomWS/Bigdaddy2166: don’t float the safety ground), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/32012 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/36138 (Bigdaddy2166: ground loop; USB isolator), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/48104 (Bigdaddy2166: EMI straps), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/17886 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/9175 (Cletus), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31460 (Holla2040), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/24052 (72Pony), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/41575 (ChelanJim), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/35218 (Wsidr1), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/43254 (Bigdaddy2166), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/45396 (nicaDd), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31161 (jamesdhatch: steel strip) Bernie’s test results # No results logged yet (as of 30 October 2026). content:
Last updated: 30 October 2026
Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads.
Applies to # A CrossFire PRO with THC and IHS (a Gen 2, FireControl machine), on a Windows computer. On my table the electronics enclosure is wall-mounted away from the table.
This is the at-startup problem: FireControl never makes a full connection. If it connects and then drops during a cut, see Scenario: connection lost or freeze mid-cut.
Versions: the threads cover FireControl 20.6 through 21.1.4. Staff in 2021–2022 asked first whether the user was on “the latest 21.1.4 version” (t/14728/13, /17). The current Windows version is 24.1.6 (downloads page, checked 2026-10-28). Doesn’t cover: Gen 1 / Mach3 CrossFires. Langmuir says those need Mach3 (PRO troubleshooting page, section 4A). Symptom (what you’ll see) # FireControl opens, but the CrossFire indicator next to ‘Machine’ stays grey, or comes and goes. A COM port number shows where the firmware version should be (ds690, t/28310/11). That’s the “not so bright” green box in t/28310/1. Sometimes Connection Help pops up after about 10 seconds. In Device Manager, ‘USB Serial Device’ is missing, or Windows reports ‘Device Descriptor Failed’. The THC may connect (its LS THC version shows) while the CrossFire won’t. What “connected” looks like (per Langmuir):
The FireControl guide says that when fully connected, the window shows ‘CrossFire’ and the firmware version (for example v1.2ls). There are two USB devices in the enclosure. Langmuir’s troubleshooting page (4E) says Device Manager should list both: the motion control board, as USB Serial Device the LS-THC, as USB-SERIAL CH340 Likely causes # Most likely first:
The USB link: cable, port, hub or extension. Langmuir says to connect “directly” (FireControl guide; troubleshooting 4C). Not connected by hand yet, or the board isn’t getting USB power. The logic boards run on USB power from the computer, even with the enclosure switch off (TinWhisperer, t/28310/3; nicaDd, t/28310/24). The main switch only powers the motors. Corrupted firmware or EEPROM. Langmuir notes that “firmware and EEPROM memory can become corrupted” (troubleshooting 4D). A damaged driver or FireControl install, often after an update or after the machine sat unused, for example over winter (staff t/14728/36; Greg9504 t/14728/45). The motion control board itself. If the same failure shows on a second computer, staff say it “may point to the MCB” (t/14728/36). Staff also say a torch or arc problem can damage the board (t/14728/43). Fixes (most to least likely) # Work down the list and stop when the CrossFire shows its firmware version.
Plug straight into the computer. The guide and troubleshooting page (4C) say to connect “directly”, with no USB extensions or hubs. Try a different USB port, then a different printer-style (USB-A to USB-B) cable. TinWhisperer gives the same advice (t/28310/6). If the cable runs to a wall-mounted enclosure, as on my table, check its whole length for damage too. Check the lights with the USB plugged in. The green light at the USB jack on the enclosure should be on (TinWhisperer, t/28310/6). Inside, the motion control board’s green LED and the THC board’s red LED should be on (JDE, t/15811/2, /4). Switch the enclosure off and unplug it from the wall before you open it. Connect by hand. Next to ‘Machine’, click Connect and choose CrossFire from the list. Its LED should turn green (troubleshooting page, section 4). If ‘CrossFire’ is greyed out with no firmware version, wait about 10 seconds for Connection Help and use it to re-flash the firmware. Then restart FireControl (troubleshooting 4D). Reinstall the driver (FireControl guide): Open Device Manager > Ports (COM & LPT). Unplug and replug the USB to see which entry is the CrossFire. Right-click it > Uninstall Device, and tick “Delete the driver software for this device”. Replug and let Windows reinstall the driver. If that fails, install the CrossFire Gen2 Driver and the THC driver by hand from the downloads page (troubleshooting 4B). Staff also suggested a driver reinstall (t/14728/36). Manual install is required on Windows 7 and 8. nicaDd’s order (t/18079/4, /10, /12, /19): Unplug the enclosure. Unzip the driver. Unzipping doesn’t install it; double-click the installer to do that. Run it as administrator. Reboot. Plug the enclosure back in, then open FireControl. Clean-reinstall FireControl. Use the PRO troubleshooting steps in Scenario: FireControl won’t open: uninstall, delete the .FireControl folder, restart, reinstall. toolboy, a long-time forum member, gives the same advice: delete the FC folder in your profile, then reinstall FireControl and the drivers (t/14728/2, /46). Write down your settings first. Try another computer. Staff: “Getting the same issue on another computer may point to the MCB” (t/14728/36). nicaDd says you can take the control box to a computer inside, because the board is USB-powered (t/28310/24). With a wall-mounted enclosure, like mine, a laptop brought to the enclosure is the easier test. Contact Langmuir support (support@langmuirsystems.com). Staff: “we can try manually re-flashing the motion control board firmware, and if that doesn’t do the trick, your motion control board will need to be replaced” (langmuir-aksel, t/14728/47). Include: FireControl version Windows version what Device Manager shows which LEDs are on what you’ve already tried JGeorgiadis’s machine was fixed by a new board (t/28310/28). Quick lookup # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) CrossFire box shows a COM port, no firmware version Not fully connected; firmware or board Fixes 3–5, then 7–8 (ds690 t/28310/11; troubleshooting 4D) CrossFire greyed out, Connection Help appears Corrupted firmware or EEPROM Re-flash from Connection Help; restart FireControl (troubleshooting 4D) No ‘USB Serial Device’ in Device Manager, or ‘Device Descriptor Failed’ Cable, port, hub, or a dead USB jack or board A different printer-style (USB-A to USB-B) cable, a different port, a different computer, then support (troubleshooting 4C, 4E; t/28310/6) THC connects (LS THC version shows) but CrossFire won’t Motion control board side Re-flash, driver, other computer, then support (t/28310; t/14728/47) Worked before; fails after an update or winter storage Driver or install damaged; sometimes the board Fixes 5–8 (staff t/14728/36; Greg9504 t/14728/45) Same failure on a second computer Motion control board Support: re-flash or replace (t/14728/36, /47) Motors hiss when the USB is unplugged Normal Nothing to fix (toolboy, t/14728/28) Where sources disagree # Driver install order. nicaDd says to install the drivers with the box unplugged, then plug it in, because “for some reason it doesn’t work the way the instructions say” (t/18079/12). It doesn’t contradict anything Langmuir says; it’s just a stricter order. Starting choice: nicaDd’s order. It costs nothing. Going back to an older FireControl (Phillipw, t/28310/18). In that thread, older versions didn’t help, and the fix was a new board (t/28310/21, /28). Starting choice: the staff order instead: current version, re-flash, driver, then support. “It’s the board.” Bigdaddy2166 tells people to get a new board: “They fail on occasion. I’m on my second one” (t/14728/53). Staff put the board after the driver, re-flash and second-computer checks (t/14728/36, /47). Starting choice: the staff order. Only buy a board after a second computer fails too. What experienced forum members add # Bigdaddy2166, t/14728/49, /51: the computer’s USB powers the control board. The 36 V DC supply powers motion through the motor drivers. If it connects but won’t move, that’s a different problem from not connecting. Greg9504, a long-time forum member, t/14728/45: a PRO that sat all winter wouldn’t connect on the same laptop, even with the green USB light on and the COM ports showing. It isn’t just new installs. Staff, t/14728/43: a torch or arc problem can damage the motion control board. If it stopped connecting right after a cutting incident, tell support. Also see Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise. Safety # Unplug the enclosure from the wall before opening it, even though the logic boards run on USB power. The 36 V supply and the mains wiring are inside. The Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) stays off for all of these checks.
Sources # Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/14728 (4,766 views, 55 posts; staff langmuirsystems #13, #17, #36, #43; langmuir-aksel #47; toolboy #2, #28, #46; Greg9504 #45; Bigdaddy2166 #49, #51, #53; TinWhisperer #55) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/28310 (marked Solved; TinWhisperer #3, #6; ds690 #11; Phillipw #18; nicaDd #24; JGeorgiadis #1, #21, #28) Forum, driver install: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/18079 (7,098 views; nicaDd #4, #10, #12, #19) Forum, LEDs: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/15811 (JDE #2, #4) Langmuir, FireControl guide (connection; driver reset): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol-guide Langmuir, PRO troubleshooting, “4: FireControl Not Connecting”: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/protroubleshooting Langmuir, downloads (Gen2 driver; THC driver): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/downloads
summary: FireControl opens, but the CrossFire indicator stays grey, shows a COM port number instead of a firmware version, or comes and goes. Causes and fixes from the computer to the drivers to the motion control board, from Langmuir’s troubleshooting page and the forum.

Last updated: 30 October 2026
Status: compiled research, not yet tried. The air chain is my setup; the checks and fixes come from Razorweld, Langmuir, and forum posts.
Applies to # My Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) on 230 V with the X45 machine torch (25 ft lead, shielded consumables) on a CrossFire PRO. My air chain is: Ingersoll-Rand SS3L3 60-gallon compressor → Ingersoll-Rand D18IN refrigerated dryer → Harbor Freight filter → the CUT45’s own rear regulator and filter cup → torch. Doesn’t cover:
Hypertherm consumable advice, SYNC cartridges, and Powermax air specs. The J45XC hand torch’s drag shield. On the CrossFire, Langmuir says to use the machine shield. Langmuir’s consumables page applies to every cutter. Where it says “check your plasma cutter’s manual”, my printed JRWPC45LH manual decides. The Razorcut 45 DI manual (a related but different model) is only a guide. Air: the numbers that come from the manufacturer # Item Value Source Set pressure 0.5 MPa (75 psi) JRWPC45LH dealer listings and the JRWPC45LT sister manual; Razorcut 45 DI manual agrees; Langmuir lists 75 psi Allowed working range 0.35–0.55 MPa (about 51–80 psi) Razorcut 45 DI manual, troubleshooting table (related model; check mine) Flow needed 190 L/min (about 6.7 CFM) JRWPC45LH dealer listings and the JRWPC45LT manual: 6.70 CFM; Razorcut 45 DI manual: 190 L/min; Langmuir: “6.7 CFM @ 75 psi” Compressor size for lots of cutting 1.5–2 x the plasma requirement, so about 10–13.4 CFM (calculated from the manual’s ratio) JRWPC45LT sister manual and Razorcut 45 DI manual Tank draining At least daily JRWPC45LT sister manual and Razorcut 45 DI manual Extra filter A submicronic particulate filter that traps water, as close as possible to the plasma air inlet JRWPC45LT sister manual and Razorcut 45 DI manual (Razorweld sells one, SKU RF50500F) Steps: checking the air system (once, then whenever cut quality drops) # Compressor capacity. Find the SS3L3’s delivered CFM at 90 psi on its nameplate or in the IR manual and compare it to 6.7 CFM (minimum) and 10–13.4 CFM (heavy cutting). SS3L3 delivered CFM: not yet recorded. Dryer capacity. Find the D18IN’s rated SCFM and its inlet temperature limit in the IR manual. The community order of parts (thread 42217) is: aftercooler (if any), then the refrigerated dryer, then the final filter or desiccant stage last, closest to the cutter. D18IN rated SCFM: not yet recorded. Order of parts. Compressor → dryer → Harbor Freight filter → final filter right at the CUT45 inlet → CUT45 regulator. The Harbor Freight filter in my chain is a mechanical filter, and Razorweld recommends a water-absorbing submicronic filter close to the cutter, so adding one there is the suggested next step. Set the pressure while air is flowing. Press the CUT45’s gas check button. Air flows until you press it again (the Razorcut 45 DI manual says it times out after 20 s; check mine). Set the rear regulator to 75 psi while it flows. Don’t go over 80 psi (0.55 MPa). mechanic416 (thread 20285, long-time forum member) runs 75–80 psi, which agrees. Drain daily: the compressor tank, the dryer drain if it’s manual, the HF filter bowl, and the CUT45’s regulator filter cup. The Razorcut 45 DI manual lists moisture in the regulator cup as a cause of an intermittent pilot arc. Moisture check. Signs of wet air: swirl marks on the cut face (thread 42217), consumables wearing fast (Langmuir), and an intermittent pilot arc (Razorcut 45 DI manual). If you see any of these, check the whole chain before touching cut settings. X45 consumables (part numbers from Langmuir, cross-checked with my copy of the torch diagram) # Diagram # Part Langmuir part no. Torch diagram says Notes 1a O-ring (on the torch head) — O-ring Not sold as an X45 consumable on Langmuir’s pages; check that it’s there and undamaged 3 Electrode RW52574 (5-pack) 52574 Replace with the nozzle 4 Swirl ring RW60041 60041 Replace if cracked, burned, or it won’t seat 5 Nozzle (cutting tip) RW51206 (5-pack) 51206, “cutting tip 20–50 amp” Replace when the hole is oval or oversized, or spatter is stuck to it 6 Retaining cap (cup) RW603505T 60305T Use RW603505T (my choice; see Where sources disagree). Don’t overtighten 7 Machine (CNC) shield RW51924 51924 Use this one on the CrossFire 9 Ohmic retaining cup — “Omic retaing cup” Not used. My PRO senses height with the IHS switch in the Z axis, not ohmic sensing My copy of the diagram is titled “TM70 or X45 CNC torch”, with an STM-70 torch head. It lists #1 torch head, #2 torch tube, and #8 torch tube with rack; those are torch body parts, not consumables.
Steps: changing consumables (order from the X45 torch diagram) # Before you start: turn the CUT45 off and let the torch cool. Follow the Razorcut 45 DI manual’s safety section for working on the torch.
Take it apart, from the outside in: CNC shield (#7), retaining cup (#6), cutting tip (#5), swirl ring (#4), electrode (#3). Inspect. Langmuir: “Worn consumables cause most cut-quality problems. Check them before you change any settings.” Nozzle: look at the orifice. Replace it if it’s oval, oversized, or has spatter stuck to it. Electrode: Langmuir says to replace it when the center pit is “about 1/16” deep on most systems", and to check the plasma cutter manual for the exact limit. The Razorcut 45 DI manual only says to replace it when the pit causes poor cuts; it gives no depth. Use 1/16 in until Razorweld says otherwise. Swirl ring: replace it if it’s cracked or burned. O-ring (#1a) on the torch head: make sure it’s in place and not cut. Change the nozzle and electrode as a pair. A new nozzle on a worn electrode wears out quickly (Langmuir). Put it back together, from the torch head outward: O-ring (#1a) checked → electrode (#3) → swirl ring (#4), fully seated → cutting tip (#5) → retaining cup (#6) → CNC shield (#7). Retaining cup: snug, not as tight as possible. Langmuir PRO troubleshooting: an overtightened X45 cap can stop the electrode moving, so the torch won’t fire a pilot arc. Torch in the mount: tighten the Machine Torch Mount’s 4 stainless screws only enough that the torch doesn’t spin. Overtightening can squeeze internal parts and cause misfires (Langmuir PRO assembly). Leave slack in the torch lead. Without slack the IHS gets pulled and errors out (Langmuir). Run the gas check and confirm 75 psi at the cutter (air steps above). Then make a short test cut before a real job. Write down the change in the results table below. Reset the running pierce count in the consumables_pierce_count column of the test-cut log. Count pierces (one per cut loop) from your programs and keep a running total between changes. How to make consumables last # From Langmuir:
Keep the air clean and dry. Use the correct pierce height. Too low wears parts. Don’t fire the torch in open air. Use THC. Change nozzle and electrode together. From Razorweld:
Don’t hold the pilot arc without cutting. Pilot arc over 2 s causes problems. What experienced forum members add # Sources are weighted as described in About this site: Langmuir first, then Razorweld/Jasic, then experienced forum members. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the CUT45.
Air
TomWS, t/27875/8 and t/10443/54: “#1 plenty of very dry air, then quality consumables”. Check pressure while cutting, not just at rest. Bigdaddy2166 (Everlast), t/43254/14: 75 psi at the machine while cutting. richarddbeck83 (Everlast), t/43254/26: pressure can collapse right after the pierce. He fixed his with a high-flow regulator and 1/2 in hose. 72Pony (CUT60), t/46610/17: use the cutter’s air test to check both static and flowing pressure. It should hold 70+ psi. Suggested: watch the CUT45 gauge during a long cut. If it drops below the DI manual’s 0.35 MPa (51 psi) range, fix the supply. Don’t just raise the setting. Compressor about to kick on. Wsidr1, t/35218/5: force the compressor on before a long cut so it doesn’t cycle mid-pierce. Compressor size. langmuir-daniel (staff), t/236: a 110 V, 26 gal compressor got him by on Razorwelds (5.6 cfm at 90 psi). shaunlb, t/236: Langmuir told him 6 cfm at 90 psi. ChelanJim, t/41575/4: 6 CFM at 90 psi, dry. These are all just under the manual’s 6.7 CFM. Size the air supply to the manual. The CUT45 regulator bowl drains itself. mechanic416 (long-time forum member), t/22679. It’s an auto-bleeder that should close at about 40 psi. Air leaking from the drain means dirt is holding the valve open. Clean it. A compressor over 135 psi can crack the bowl. Phillipw: a leak isn’t normal. toolboy (long-time forum member; Everlast), t/28381/41: 3/8 in air line minimum. Watch the desiccant color. Drain the tank. Let the post-flow run (he says 30 s or more) before shutting off, so the torch cools. The CUT45 runs its own post-flow; don’t cut power right after a job. Aftercooler. brownfox (long-time forum member), t/8504/1: an aftercooler ahead of the dryer cuts the water load. Dryer placement. gamblegarage, t/236: put the dryer close to the cutter. Consumables
Use the full matched stack from one maker. mechanic416 (long-time forum member), t/25275/61: electrode, tip, swirl ring, retaining cup, and shield. Mixing brands caused misfires. He also got poor cuts on low supply voltage (200 V). The X45 tip. mechanic416, t/21266: 1.0 mm, rated 45–50 A, 0.040 in orifice. It’s the only tip offered for that torch. Kerf at least 0.055 in. toolboy (same thread) cuts 1/4 in down to 24 ga with it. How long a set lasts. ChelanJim (Hypertherm 45XP), t/32592/1, quoting Hypertherm: About 2–3 hours of arc-on time hand cutting, 3–5 hours machine cutting. In machine cutting the electrode usually wears out first. That’s a Hypertherm figure for a different torch, so it’s a rough expectation, not an X45 spec. Spares and stacking. ChelanJim, t/37146/1: Keep about half a dozen nozzle and electrode sets, plus swirl rings. Never use knock-offs. Keep a chart of how the stack goes together (the torch diagram does this). Replace parts before they ruin a job. TomWS, t/30637/6. Bigdaddy2166, t/43254/14: new, genuine consumables (not knock-offs). What kills tips. gamblegarage (long-time forum member), t/236: Long pilot-arc time. Wet air. Wrong cut height. Piercing too-thick plate with the torch low (molten blow-back). Running more amps than the orifice is made for. Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Consumables wear out fast Water or oil in the air; pierce height too low; firing in open air Fix the air chain; pierce height (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height) (Langmuir) Pilot arc cuts in and out Moisture or dirt in the air; pressure too high; pilot arc over 2 s; worn parts Drain the regulator cup; set 0.35–0.55 MPa; replace consumables (Razorcut 45 DI manual) Torch won’t fire a pilot arc Retaining cap too tight; worn electrode; debris in the electrode spring Loosen the cap slightly; replace parts; work the spring (Langmuir PRO troubleshooting, THC guide) No pilot arc at all Cutter left in gas check mode Press gas check again or wait 20 s (Razorcut 45 DI manual) Wide or wandering kerf Worn nozzle; low air pressure Replace the nozzle; check the regulator (Langmuir) Swirl marks on the cut face Moisture Drain, dryer, final filter (thread 42217) Marks on the tip Often pilot-arc strikes Check pierce height and the arc-start sequence (thread 44335) Bevel and extra dross on parts that used to be clean Worn nozzle Replace the nozzle and electrode (Langmuir) Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # Air pressure 75 vs. 85 psi. Beefmaster (t/22679#5) says Razorweld phone support told him 85 psi. JRWPC45LH dealer listings say 0.5 MPa (75 psi), the Razorcut 45 DI manual says 75 psi with 51–80 psi allowed, and Langmuir says 75. Starting choice: 75 psi (written manufacturer data beats a second-hand phone call). If you try higher, keep it under 80. Air flow. JRWPC45LH dealer listings say 6.70 CFM, the Razorcut 45 DI manual says 190 L/min, and Langmuir says 6.7 CFM. Those match. The J45XC torch sheet lists 100 L/min (3.55 cfm), but that’s the hand torch. Size the air to 6.7 CFM (the whole cutter’s requirement, from two manufacturer sources). Air pressure. J45XC sheet: 65–75 psi. Razorcut 45 DI manual: 75 psi set, 51–80 psi allowed. mechanic416: 75–80 psi. Starting choice: 75 psi. That’s the JRWPC45LH spec, the DI manual, and Langmuir agreeing, and it stays inside every range listed. How long consumables last. There’s no Razorweld or Langmuir figure. ChelanJim quotes Hypertherm: 3–5 h of arc-on time machine cutting (t/32592/1). Thread 44335 quotes 600–900 pierces for a Powermax45. Both are Hypertherm numbers for a different torch. Use 3–5 h only as a rough expectation, and track your own arc-on time and pierce counts. Tip amp rating and size. My copy of the torch diagram labels the 51206 cutting tip “20–50 amp”. That covers the CUT45’s full 20–45 A range on 230 V, so it should be fine at 45 A. Orifice size: mechanic416 (long-time forum member, t/21266) says the X45 tip is 1.0 mm (0.040 in), 45–50 A, the only tip offered. The Razorcut 45 DI manual’s general advice says 1.0 mm for 0–40 A. Neither Razorweld nor Langmuir states the X45 orifice. Working answer: 1.0 mm / 0.040 in (community, but it agrees with the diagram’s 20–50 A rating). Worth confirming with Razorweld if it ever matters. Retaining cup part number (decided). Langmuir’s X45 retaining cap listing says RW603505T. My copy of the diagram says 60305T. My choice: treat the diagram’s 60305T as a typo; the part to order is RW603505T. New evidence (October 2026): Razorweld’s torch-parts sheet for my model (JRWPC45LH, HYP45 hand torch) also lists the retaining cap as RW60305T, alongside the same RW51206 nozzle, RW52574 electrode, and RW60041 swirl ring as the X45. So 60305T may be Razorweld’s own number, not a typo. I’m still ordering Langmuir’s listed RW603505T; worth checking with Langmuir if the numbers ever matter.
