Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads.
Applies to # A CrossFire PRO with THC and IHS, with FireControl on a Windows computer. On my table the electronics enclosure is wall-mounted away from the table.
Electrical noise (EMI) and grounding are the most common cause of mid-cut dropouts, and they have their own page: Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise. Work through that page first. This page is for what’s left after it: the computer, the USB link, Windows power settings, and the FireControl install. To pick the job back up afterwards, see Scenario: resuming a cut. Versions: the reports span FireControl 20.5 to 21.1.5 on Windows 10 and 11. A 2025 XR report (t/42107) doesn’t give a version, and the replies there treat it as noise (TinWhisperer #2, Sticks #3). The fixes below don’t depend on the version, except where noted. Symptom (what you’ll see) # A cut stops part-way. FireControl freezes, goes blank, or says “Machine disconnected” or “Program cancelled”. The THC or the machine is lost after a pause or overnight. Jogging is laggy, or keys act late. A Java error (java.lang.NullPointerException … ThcConfiguration …) appears, then the job drops to a hold, often during the IHS probe. FireControl closes itself mid-cut. In the worst case, motion freezes with the arc still on (t/16264/1). See Safety below. Likely causes # Most likely first:
Electrical noise (EMI) from the arc. The most common cause; see the grounding page. Windows power saving: the computer sleeps or turns off the USB device (jamesdhatch, t/7850/2; Bigdaddy2166, t/39348/9). A Windows update can switch a power setting back on (brownfox, t/39348/6). The USB link: a loose plug at the control box or a bad solder joint on the USB connector (jindano, t/39348/16; TomWS, t/39348/17), a worn cable or port, or a USB cable routed against the table frame (t/24624/78, /81). The computer itself: bad USB ports (Fortifyfabworks, t/16264/19), or an old computer that can’t run the current FireControl (rmeyers, t/28606/9, /11). The FireControl install: a stale .FireControl folder, “especially after switching between versions” (langmuirsystems, t/22160/6), or FireControl left open and idle too long (t/24624/59; t/12629/20). Something closed FireControl: a Windows update in the background (t/26056/44–45) or the window’s X clicked by accident (t/33962/15). Fixes (most to least likely) # 1. Find out whether it’s noise or the computer # JA6’s isolation test (t/16264/17). Welder6131 ran it in the same thread, found a bad laptop, and was “up and running” again (#20, #21).
Switch the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) off and unplug it. Dry-run the same file that has been failing. Still fails with the plasma unplugged? Then it isn’t plasma noise. Go to fix 2. Only fails with the arc on? It’s noise. Go back to the grounding page. Swap computers and dry-run again. If it fails only with the arc on, try a run with THC off as a diagnostic step (JA6, #17). It’s not a fix; see THC setup. 2. Stop the computer sleeping and turning off USB # jamesdhatch, a long-time forum member, t/7850/2: if the laptop sleeps, it “loses the connection to the THC”. Restarting FireControl doesn’t fix it; you have to unplug and replug the USB. He made a separate Windows power profile for the CrossFire that never sleeps. Bigdaddy2166, t/39348/9, after a “Machine disconnect” report: In Settings > System > Power & battery, choose a performance power mode instead of a power-saving one. In Device Manager, right-click the USB device > Properties > Power Management, and untick “Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power.” brownfox, a long-time forum member, t/39348/6: a Windows update can switch a power setting back on. Check these again after big Windows updates. 3. Fix the USB link # Plug in directly with a sound cable and a tight plug. The guide says no extensions or hubs. jindano’s “Machine disconnect” turned out to be a loose USB plug at the control box (t/39348/16). TomWS says it may be a bad solder joint on the USB connector (t/39348/17). A different cable or a different port on the computer is the first swap (Bigdaddy2166, t/39348/2). PixelTamer (t/39348/18): packing a loose plug with foil is “a poor solution”. Fix or replace the connector. Keep the USB cable off the table frame. Wsidr1 stopped running the cable through the laptop-tray hole and had no more freezes in 6–8 signs (t/24624/78). RAMtech marked his thread solved after moving the USB cables away from the frame (t/24624/81). With a wall-mounted enclosure, like mine, check where the USB run between the computer and the enclosure touches metal. 4. Test the jog, and restart FireControl before cutting # Wsidr1, t/24624/59: press the arrow keys a few times. If there’s a delay, close and reopen FireControl, or restart the computer. “If I get good jog function repeatedly, I never have a freeze up when cutting.” 72Pony, t/12629/20: doesn’t leave FireControl open and idle. If he isn’t using it, he closes it. 5. Suspect the computer # USB ports. Fortifyfabworks’s freezes were the laptop’s USB ports, and his USB mouse misbehaved too. He bought a cheap laptop just for the table (t/16264/19). Java error, then lost connection (often during the IHS probe). rmeyers got java.lang.NullPointerException … ThcConfiguration …, and the job dropped to a hold, always during the G38 probe (t/28606/1, /3). It was fixed by a newer computer running the newest FireControl. His old PC “could not support it graphically” (t/28606/9, /11). 6. Clean up the FireControl install # Slow, laggy, or stuck jogging: staff say to delete the .FireControl folder, “especially after switching between versions” (langmuirsystems, t/22160/6). Then reinstall (steps in Scenario: FireControl won’t open). Install the current version (24.1.6 on Windows) unless you have a reason not to. On older graphics hardware, use the 21.1.5-compatibility build (downloads page). 7. Keep anything from closing FireControl mid-job # No Windows updates while cutting. jamesdhatch (t/26056/45): updates in the background can kill a running FireControl. DnKFab lost a 40-minute cut that way (t/26056/44). Don’t touch the close-window X while a job runs. holla2040 hit it by accident mid-cut, and FireControl “promptly quit” (t/33962/15). Recovering when it hangs # FireControl guide: The circular reset icon next to the connection resets the connection and auto-connects again. It’s for clearing an alarm “or if the machine is unresponsive”. “Your XY position may be lost if you reset or disconnect while the machine is in motion.” Before you resume, check the work zero against the part (jog the torch over a cut you know). Then follow Scenario: resuming a cut. Quick lookup # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Freezes only with the arc on Electrical noise Grounding page; isolation test (t/16264/17) Freezes in a dry run with the plasma unplugged Computer, USB, or install Swap computers (t/16264/20–21); fixes 2–6 Lost THC or machine after a pause or overnight Computer slept or turned off the USB Never-sleep power profile; untick USB power saving (t/7850/2; t/39348/9) “Machine disconnect” from a fussy plug Loose USB at the control box; bad connector joint Reseat; repair or replace the connector (t/39348/16–17) Laggy jog, keys acted on late Install or folder problem; FireControl open too long Delete .FireControl, reinstall (t/22160/6); restart FC before cutting (t/24624/59) Java NullPointerException, then a hold during IHS Old computer can’t run the current FC Newer computer and the newest FC (t/28606/9, /11) “Program cancelled” mid-cut USB cable against the frame Re-route the USB (t/24624/81) FireControl closed itself mid-cut Window X clicked, or Windows update Keep clear of the X; pause updates (t/33962/15; t/26056/44–45) Where sources disagree # Laptop on battery vs. 3-to-2-prong “cheater” plugs. nicaDd (t/16264/2), toolboy (t/12629/9, /14) and jamesdhatch (t/12629/10) suggest a 3-to-2 adapter or cutting off the ground prong. That defeats a safety ground, and TomWS and Bigdaddy2166 call floating the safety ground “craziness” (grounding page, t/24659/16). Don’t do it. Run the laptop on battery, or use a USB ground-loop isolator (see the grounding page). Staying on an old version (nicaDd on 20.5, t/24624/49; Bill_A on 20.6.2, t/22160/2). Staff suggest a clean .FireControl folder and a current install (t/22160/6). rmeyers’s fix included the newest version (t/28606/11). Starting choice: staff’s advice, current version first. Ground rod for the frame (Bigdaddy2166, t/24624/42, /75; RAMtech #81). That’s a grounding question; follow the grounding page, not this page. What experienced forum members add # Wsidr1, t/24624/59: test the jog every time; if it’s slow, restart FireControl, and sometimes the computer. 72Pony, t/12629/20: close FireControl when you’re not using it. TomWS, t/39348/14: if the metal rim of the USB plug touches the enclosure, “that would definitely cause interference problems”. Fortifyfabworks, t/16264/19: a cheap laptop just for the table, with CAD on another computer. Safety # If the motion freezes with the arc still on (t/16264/1), switch the CUT45 off at the cutter first. Then deal with FireControl. Don’t put hands near the torch until the cutter is off. Never defeat a safety ground to fix noise (see the grounding page). Follow Langmuir’s safety page and my CUT45 manual.
Sources # Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/16264 (2,467 views; Welder6131 #1, #20, #21; nicaDd #2; JA6 #17; Fortifyfabworks #19) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/28606 (solved; rmeyers #1, #3, #9, #11) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/24624 (81 posts, solved; Bigdaddy2166 #42, #75; nicaDd #49; Wsidr1 #59, #78; RAMtech #81) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/39348 (Bigdaddy2166 #2, #9; brownfox #6; TomWS #14, #17; jindano #16; PixelTamer #18) Forum, sleep drops the THC: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/7850/2 (jamesdhatch) Forum, lag fixed by deleting the folder: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/22160 (Bill_A #2, #5; langmuirsystems #6) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12629 (toolboy #9, #14; jamesdhatch #10; 72Pony #20) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/26056 (DnKFab #44; jamesdhatch #45); https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/33962/15 (holla2040); https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/42107 (XR with a Cut60; TinWhisperer #2; Sticks #3) Langmuir, FireControl guide (reset connection; XY may be lost; plug in directly): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol-guide Langmuir, downloads: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/downloads
summary: A cut stops part-way: FireControl freezes, goes blank, says “Machine disconnected” or “Program cancelled”, or throws a Java error. Electrical noise is the usual suspect and has its own page. This page covers the computer, USB, power-saving, and FireControl-install causes, plus a test to tell them apart.

Status: Razorweld chart settings used by me, not formally tested. Everything else on this page is compiled research, not yet tried.
Applies to # My Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) on 230 V (20–45 A; the JRWPC45LH is a 230 V single-phase machine, and the 120 V figures in the Razorcut 45 DI manual are for that dual-voltage model) with the X45 machine torch, the 51206 “20–50 amp” tip, and the machine shield, on a CrossFire PRO with IHS and THC (300 ipm max). Materials: mild steel, stainless, and aluminum, mostly 3/16 in and thinner. Doesn’t cover:
Hypertherm, Everlast, and Primeweld charts as settings. The T45m-format chart below is in, because FSFab reports Jasic supplied it for the CUT45. Numbers from experienced members on other cutters (Everlast, PrimeWeld CUT60, Hypertherm) are rough guides only. The “Razorcut 45 chart” in forum thread 10695 (since removed from the forum), which a long-time forum member says is for the older IPT-style torch. Any 120 V figures. TM70 / X45 CNC torch parts diagram: 52574 electrode, 60041 swirl ring, 51206 cutting tip (20–50 A), 60305T retaining cup, 51924 CNC shield. Tap to enlarge. I couldn’t find an X45 machine-torch cut chart published by Langmuir (Langmuir pages checked in 2026; thread 11738). My starting chart is manufacturer data that came via the forum: Razorweld sent it to forum member MO-Hacker, who posted it on 2019-09-20: “Here is the cut chart that Razorweld sent me for the 45” (https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/847/29). PWCNC (t/847/45) and TinWhisperer (t/21266/8) reposted it. I’ve cut with these settings and they worked well, but they haven’t been formally tested on my machine yet. The test-cut program is the plan for that.
Which Razorweld manual applies # My cutter is the Razorweld CUT45 CNC, model JRWPC45LH (“CNC - CROSSFIRE COMPATIBLE” on the manual cover, built by Jasic). Langmuir sells it as the “Razorweld Razorcut 45 with Machine Torch”, and Langmuir’s Reference page links the Razorcut 45 DI manual (2022) under that name. That DI manual is for a related but different model: it’s dual-voltage (120/230 V), lists 25 % duty cycle, and has error codes and a Mesh mode. My printed JRWPC45LH manual has none of the DI manual’s residential-supply warning in its safety section. I couldn’t find the JRWPC45LH manual online. The closest published documents are the manual for its sister model JRWPC45LT (same CUT45 machine with a hand torch; Razorweld’s spec sheet lists both codes), Razorweld’s JRWPC45LH torch-parts sheet, and dealer spec listings. On this page, figures from the DI manual are labeled as such. Check them against my printed manual before relying on them.
Cover of my printed manual: Razorweld JRWPC45LH, “CNC – CrossFire compatible.” Tap to enlarge. How sources are weighted on this page:
Langmuir docs and staff: heights, THC, and machine limits. Razorweld data: my printed JRWPC45LH manual (not yet typed in here), the Razorcut 45 DI manual (a related but different model; a rough hand-cutting table, only two thicknesses), and this Razorweld-supplied chart (Razorweld to MO-Hacker). For machine settings I start from the chart and use the manual as a sanity check. The T45m-format chart reportedly supplied by Jasic (FSFab, t/45011). It’s a second candidate set, to be tested side by side in the test-cut program. Its Jasic origin is unconfirmed. Experienced forum members, then everyone else. Caveats from the forum about the Razorweld chart:
PWCNC (t/847/30): the CrossFire only goes 300 ipm, and “I still make my own, test cut all material first”. TinWhisperer (t/21266/8): a good start only; machines vary a lot unit to unit. Another 847 poster says its speeds don’t suit the CrossFire. The chart doesn’t name a torch, and it’s from 2019. It’s assumed here to fit the X45 machine torch; the test-cut program is meant to confirm or reject that. Razorweld chart (my starting settings) # Source: Razorweld, via forum member MO-Hacker (t/847/29). Status: used by me, worked well, not formally tested.
Typed in from my saved image of the chart (view image) and checked cell by cell against the forum copy on 28 October 2026: every ipm, voltage, delay, and amps value matches. Use the Optimum column as the starting feed. “Max” is the fastest the chart says will still sever the metal, not a quality speed. ⚠ marks speeds over the PRO’s 300 ipm limit, which the PRO can’t reach. “—” means the chart gives no pierce delay.
The chart gives no cut height, pierce height, air pressure, or kerf. It may be a typing error in Razorweld’s original. Trust the 221 optimum only after a ladder test, and ignore the 640.

stainless 22 ga optimum shows 6179 mm/min, but 322 ipm = 8179; aluminum 3/32 optimum shows 4626, but 190 ipm = 4826; smaller slips on mild 16 ga max, aluminum 1/16 max, 1/8 max, and 1/4 max. Use the ipm columns only.

No cut height, pierce height, PSI, kerf, or consumable list. The chart can’t be copied whole. Those settings come from the other procedure pages (air, pierce height, kerf).
The chart tops out at 40 A, though my cutter can do 45 A. Razorweld’s rule says full output on thick material (see Where sources disagree).
Amps don’t follow thickness the same way in each material. Stainless jumps to 40 A at 18 ga; mild steel stays at 25 A through 16 ga. That’s why stainless 18 ga (335 ipm) is “faster” than mild 18 ga (203 ipm).
Arc voltages are 139–152 V. That’s at or above the top of Langmuir’s “typical 60–150 V” (and the THC guide’s 90–150 V). It’s still inside the flowchart’s 85–230 V “in range” and well under the 280 V that can damage the THC. Arc voltage depends on torch height, and the chart doesn’t give one.

Amps don’t mean the same thing on a different torch. The forum also keeps a shared Google Sheet (“Razorweld Cut Chart”; threads 18563 and 8921): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/12SPhiHimP9lWIOJTGaHhDAiaQoUz5Hq0YjbL92mMBSo. Its contents haven’t been checked for this site. Open it and check before using any number from it. This chart says 111–123 V for 3/16 in and thinner, at a stated 0.06 in torch-to-work distance. The Razorweld chart says 139–152 V, with no height given. Row for row, they’re about 20–40 V apart. Arc voltage rises as the torch goes up (THC guide; Cletus), so either Razorweld’s numbers were taken higher off the plate or one chart is for a different torch. Don’t type either voltage into FireControl as fact. The test-cut program is planned to test both against SMART voltage, and measure the real torch height, before either is picked.
Where it comes from.
FSFab posted these charts in https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/45011 (2025-08-13). He says Jasic supplied them for the CUT45 machine torch. Jasic builds the CUT45. He ran the 3/16 in settings on an XR with a CUT45 machine torch. They cured a “pierces, then torch goes out” problem; he cut three test pieces start to finish. Phillipw replied that they’re “very close to Hypertherm spec”. Origin not confirmed. FSFab’s post says Jasic supplied this chart, but its layout, the “T45m shielded consumables” label, and the 400 ipm test-table footnote match Hypertherm’s Powermax45 charts. It’s a second candidate setting set, no longer reference only. It’s weighted below the Razorweld chart (origin unconfirmed; one tester, a general forum member), and above other forum numbers. The test-cut program runs its voltage as T2 in every session. There’s also an optional session comparing its 45 A, 3/16 mild steel settings against the Razorweld chart. For example: 3/16 mild steel: 147 V vs. 118 V. 16 ga mild steel: 152 V vs. 116 V at 45 A or 111 V at 30 A. The amps don’t match the Razorweld chart’s 25 A. Pierce delays run short on Langmuir tables. Greg9504 (t/12941/2, also t/8193) quotes Langmuir staff: FireControl times the pierce delay from the torch-on command, not from arc-on. Book values like these assume arc-on, so add the time the arc takes to start. Treat this chart’s delays as a minimum. They’re already shorter than the Razorweld chart’s: 0.5 vs. 0.75 s on 3/16 mild, 0.1 vs. 0.25 s on 14 ga mild. Short version:
Fresh or known-good consumables, 75 psi at the gas check, clean dry air (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables). Clean flat scrap. Set the chart amps on the CUT45 knob (FireControl doesn’t set amps; Langmuir staff, thread 5883). Speed ladder around the chart optimum: −20 %, −10 %, 0, +10 %, +20 %. Capped at 300 ipm. Watch the arc under the plate (with eye protection; see Safety). Razorweld: the arc should leave the bottom “at a slight angle away from the direction of travel”. Straight down means too slow, with dross build-up. Sparks spraying up on top means too fast, or not enough amps. Grade dross, bevel, and top spatter. Langmuir: slow cuts leave heavy dross on the bottom; fast cuts leave small beads. Then test pierce delay, check the THC voltage, and measure the kerf on the winning setting (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height; THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives; Kerf width and hole/part accuracy). Log every coupon in the test-cut log. Put the winner in the results table below and in a SheetCAM tool with the amps in the tool name (SheetCAM 8.0 setup for FireControl). Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Heavy, bubbly dross on the bottom; arc goes straight down Too slow Raise the feed 10 % at a time (Razorweld, Langmuir) Sparks up on top, small hard beads on the bottom, not cut through Too fast, or amps too low Slow down, or raise the amps (Razorweld, Langmuir) Wide kerf and rough edge on thin sheet Too many amps for thin material Turn the amps down (Razorweld tips) Chart speed is over 300 ipm PRO’s limit Lower the amps and ladder-test at ≤300 ipm (Razorweld thin-material rule) Results drift worse over a session Nozzle wearing, wet air Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables Can’t match the chart speed Machine differences (Bigdaddy2166, thread 44500) Trust your ladder test, not the chart Duty cycle # At 45 A, JRWPC45LH dealer listings, the JRWPC45LT manual (the sister model: same CUT45 machine, sold with a different torch), and Langmuir all give 30 % at 45 A (at 104 °F). The 25 % figure used here before came from the Razorcut 45 DI manual, a different model. Check the duty cycle in my printed manual; until I have, I plan on the more conservative 25 % and rest the cutter between long 45 A cuts. If the cutter overheats (the JRWPC45LT manual shows an overheat light; the DI shows error codes E60/E61), leave the machine switched on so the fan cools it, and wait for it to clear (both Razorweld manuals).
Safety # Plasma arc light, fumes, and fire are covered by my JRWPC45LH manual’s safety section and Langmuir’s safety page. Langmuir: never cut materials coated with paint, oil, grease, or solvents, and consult the MSDS. Razorweld: read the MSDS for the metal and any coating, and use ventilation or fume extraction. Galvanized or coated stock: follow those documents. This page doesn’t cover it. Use eye protection to ANSI Z87.1 / Z49.1 (Langmuir).
Fixed settings on the cutter # Amps are set on the CUT45 knob. FireControl doesn’t control amps (Langmuir staff, thread 5883). Write the amps in the CAM tool name so you remember to set them. Air: 75 psi (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables). Trigger mode: check which mode your cutter is set to; 2T is assumed in the sources. The Razorcut 45 DI manual (a related model) describes 4T as latching and holding a pilot arc, plus a Mesh mode. The JRWPC45LT manual (the sister model: same CUT45 machine, sold with a different torch) shows only 2T and 4T on the front panel, so my CUT45 may not have Mesh; check my panel and manual. Langmuir doesn’t say which mode to use with the CNC; 2T is the usual assumption because it simply follows the table’s on/off signal. Confirm with Langmuir (it’s on my list of support questions). Amps: start from the Razorweld chart (25 A on thin sheet, 40 A from 14 ga up). Razorweld’s general rule (in the JRWPC45LT manual (the sister model: same CUT45 machine, sold with a different torch) and in the DI manual) is: “On thick material, set the machine to full output and vary your travel speed. On thinner material… turn down the amperage.” That suggests 45 A for 3/16 in and 1/4 in, while the chart says 40 A. See Conflicts. Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # Razorweld chart vs. Razorcut 45 DI manual vs. T45m/Jasic chart vs. forum. The Razorweld chart and the manual are both Razorweld data, and they mostly agree where they overlap. The chart is the more complete one for machine cutting, so ladders start from its Optimum column, with the manual used as a sanity check (and as the start for 3/16 aluminum). The T45m/Jasic chart is the second candidate (the test-cut program’s T2 and the optional 45 A session). Forum numbers are weighted last. All of it is unverified until the test-cut program’s results are logged. 16 ga mild steel speed. Chart 114 vs. Cletus 150 vs. thread 847 72. A ±20 % ladder from 114 covers 91–137. If the best rung is at either end, run a second ladder beyond it. 1/8 aluminum. Chart 133 vs. thread 847’s about 45. Too far apart to both be right for the same setup. Test from 133 and go down if needed. The 847 shorthand is unverified. Amps on thick material. Chart 40 A vs. Razorweld’s “full output on thick material” (45 A). Starting choice: the chart’s 40 A. If 3/16 shows dross at every rung, try one ladder at 45 A. Arc voltage. Chart 139–152 V vs. the community 115–128 V (thread 38627, an XR owner) vs. Langmuir’s “typical 60–150 V” and the CUT45’s rated output voltage (96–98 V, depending on the Razorweld document). Don’t type chart voltages into FireControl as fact. SMART voltage stays the default (Langmuir staff, thread 5883). The test-cut program compares a fixed chart voltage to the SMART reading. Arc voltage, T45m/Jasic vs. Razorweld chart (the big one). T45m: 111–123 V at 0.06 in (3/16 and under). Razorweld: 139–152 V at an unstated height. Both claim to be for the CUT45. Planned 3-way test in the test-cut program: the SMART reading, the Razorweld chart’s voltage (T1), and the T45m chart’s voltage for that thickness (T2), with the real torch height measured. Duty cycle: JRWPC45LH dealer listings, the JRWPC45LT sister manual, and Langmuir: 30 % at 45 A. Razorcut 45 DI manual (2022, a different model): 25 %. Thread 236’s “older manual” (30 % at 45 A, 20–40 A output) matches the JRWPC45LT manual. Starting choice: my printed manual’s figure; until I’ve checked it, plan on 25 %. Jasic charts. Thread 45011 (FSFab): the T45m-format charts above, now a candidate in the test-cut program. Thread 44500: a search-result summary (not checked against the full thread) suggests those heights were for Jasic’s own CNC torch. Not used. Pierce delays. Razorweld chart: 0.25–1.00 s on 40 A rows, none on 25 A rows. T45m/Jasic: 0.0–0.9 s, and it runs short on FireControl, which starts timing at the torch-on command (staff via Greg9504, t/12941/2). Starting choice: the Razorweld chart’s delays, then test them (the test-cut program). Applies to # A CrossFire PRO with THC and IHS, running SheetCAM programs (Langmuir post) in FireControl.
Versions: “Run From Line” arrived in FireControl 20.5 (staff, t/10840/2). The fixes below match the guide for the current interface. Most forum reports are on 21.1.4–21.1.5. Related: Indexing long parts uses Run From Here on purpose, to cut a part longer than the table. This page is for recovering from an unplanned stop. If the stop was a frozen or dropped connection, fix that first: Scenario: connection lost or freeze mid-cut. Practise on scrap before you need it: start a small two-part program, stop it during the first part, and recover it. Symptom (what you’ll see) # A cut stopped part-way: the torch went out, a consumable failed, or you paused or stopped mid-sheet. Resume faults with “retry the path”. FireControl says it can’t start in the middle of a loop. The restarted cut lands in the wrong place. The orange Loop/Line button does nothing, or Run From Line moves but doesn’t cut. After an M00 planned pause, the Torch Enable switch is greyed out. Likely causes # Most likely first:
Paused or stopped in the middle of a cut (torch on). Resume only works between cuts (FireControl guide; 72Pony, t/28506/2, /4). The work zero changed: Zero All Axes pressed, or the torch or sheet moved (DonP, t/30573/2, /5). Dry Run left on, so the orange button does nothing or the restart “acts as a dry run” (Simsworx, t/31759/7). XY position lost by a reset during motion (guide) or by a reinstall (brownfox, t/30573/9). A FireControl version problem with the button (ChelanJim, t/31759/4; fixed on 21.1.4, #8). A hardware fault, rarely: one 2026 user later replaced his motion control board (strongautoandfab, t/10840/7, /9). How FireControl thinks about it (per Langmuir) # From the FireControl guide:
Pause between cuts (for example during a rapid move), and you can carry on with Resume. Pause or stop in the middle of a cut (torch on), and you can’t simply resume. “Note the current g-code line and use this to pick up the cut again using the ‘Run From Here’ feature.” “FireControl automatically stores your work position when pausing and stopping programs.” “Since a cut program cannot start in the middle of a cut loop, FireControl will automatically determine the start of the cutting loop” and ask you to confirm. Afterwards, the visualizer doesn’t show the loops before the restart point. Keys: Alt+R start, Space Bar pause, Alt+S stop. Loop vs. line (toolboy and brownfox, t/14626/2, /4; TinWhisperer, t/10840/4, /5):
A loop is one whole torch-on, cut, torch-off path, from pierce to the end of that cut. Run From Loop re-pierces at the start of that path and cuts all of it again. A line is a piece of that path. Run From Line starts part-way along it. TinWhisperer says it writes in a new pierce at that point (t/10840/4). Fixes (most to least likely) # 1. Recover with Run From Here after a torch-out or mid-cut stop # Make it safe. If the motion stopped with the arc on, switch the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) off. Fix the cause: consumables (Air and X45 consumables), grounding, or the arc-loss settings (THC setup). Don’t move the sheet. Don’t press “Zero All Axes”. DonP: zeroing again “will create new starting point”, and you have to restart from the original work zero (t/30573/2, /5). ChelanJim: this only works if FireControl still shows the part, you haven’t moved the torch or sheet, and the settings are intact (t/37966/4). Note the line. Before clearing the alarm, write down the G-code line FireControl was on (guide). If you missed it, click the spot in the visualizer where the cut stopped. It jumps to that code line (brownfox, t/14626/4; TinWhisperer, t/30573/3). Choose Loop or Line. The orange button on that line offers Run From Loop or Run From Line. If FireControl says it can’t start mid-loop, accept the loop start it offers (guide; t/10840). Loop: the safer choice for a small part, or when the miss is near the start of a cut. The whole profile is cut again; the already-cut part just gets a second pass. Line: use it on a long profile, to start just before where the cut stopped. Expect a pierce mark where it restarts. Confirm “generate”. FireControl asks whether to generate the program from that point. Say yes (ChelanJim, t/37966/4; DonP, t/30573/2). Go to Work Zero, then Start. ChelanJim’s order (t/37966/4): generate, Go to Work Zero, Start. Before Go to Work Zero, check the DRO for a clear path (guide). Watch the first pierce and be ready to stop. 2. If the restart lands in the wrong place # Return to the original work zero; don’t re-zero (DonP, t/30573/2, /5). If XY was lost after a freeze, reset or reinstall, re-find the zero on a known feature. Without limit switches there’s no home to fall back on (brownfox, t/30573/9).
3. If the orange Loop/Line button does nothing, or the restart doesn’t cut # Turn Dry Run off (Simsworx, t/31759/7). Then try another listed FireControl version (ChelanJim, t/31759/4; A7MOSPHERIC fixed it on 21.1.4, #8). If Start stays grey after you pick the line, try Go to Work Zero (ChelanJim, t/30573/17). It didn’t help OkieBuckeye in that case (#18). If it still moves without cutting, suspect hardware: strongautoandfab later replaced his motion control board (t/10840/7, /9). 4. After a planned pause (M00), for scribing or swapping tools # M00 works; M01 doesn’t. jamesdhatch, a long-time forum member: “Use M00. M01 requires an optional stop switch” (t/8048/2). Resuming after M00 (2026 reports): poppabear (t/48685/17, /21) and rat196426 (t/48685/9, /12, /16) both say the torch does fire again when you carry on. The Torch Enable switch stays greyed out, but the torch-on indicator at the bottom and the table itself show it firing. poppabear calls it a display bug. poppabear’s two posts differ on the button: #17 says “the pause button, then the Start button”; #21 says “Resume”. rat196426 says hit Start, not Resume. Try Start first, on scrap. Simpler option: ds690 suggests separate gouge or scribe and cut files (t/48685/7). Older versions: on 20.6.2, users reported FireControl froze after M00 (t/13735/1), and nicaDd had “no success” with it (t/23300/5). Quick lookup # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Resume faults with “retry the path” Paused in the middle of a cut Run From Line or Loop instead (72Pony, t/28506/2, /4; guide) “Can’t start in the middle of a loop” Expected behavior Accept the loop start FireControl offers (guide; t/10840) Restarted cut lands in the wrong place Work zero changed (Zero All Axes, torch moved, or sheet moved) Return to the original work zero; don’t re-zero (DonP, t/30573/2, /5) Orange Loop/Line button does nothing Dry Run on; version problem Turn Dry Run off (Simsworx, t/31759/7); try another listed version (ChelanJim, t/31759/4; fixed on 21.1.4, #8) Lost position after a freeze, reset, or restart XY lost by a reset during motion (guide), or by a reinstall Re-find the zero on a known feature. Without limit switches there’s no home to fall back on (brownfox, t/30573/9) Run From Line moves but doesn’t cut (“acts as a dry run”) Dry Run left on, or a hardware fault Check the Dry Run toggle (t/31759/7). That 2026 user later replaced his motion control board (strongautoandfab, t/10840/7, /9) Torch Enable greyed after M00 Display bug Press Start; the torch fires anyway (t/48685/17, /21) Where sources disagree # Pause = stop? In 2021, MotoRider42HC reported that Pause acted like Stop mid-cut (t/12401/1). jamesdhatch says CNC machines don’t agree on what pause should do (#6). The guide spells out the current behavior: resume between cuts, Run From Here mid-cut. The guide’s behavior is used here. Pause between cuts when you can. Older version to fix the button. A7MOSPHERIC fixed the dead button with 21.1.4 (t/31759/8), while OkieBuckeye’s 2025 attempts didn’t help (t/30573/18). It’s a workaround; there’s no staff answer. Check Dry Run first, then the version. M00 on resume. 2021–2022 reports say it freezes on 20.6.2. 2026 reports say it works with the greyed-out switch. The 2026 reports are used here for current versions. Test on scrap before relying on it for a real job. What experienced forum members add # 72Pony, t/28506/2, /4: “In the future if you need to pause do it between cuts.” ChelanJim, t/30573/17: if Start stays grey after you pick the line, try Go to Work Zero. It didn’t help OkieBuckeye in that case (#18). brownfox, a long-time forum member, t/30573/9: an uninstall and reinstall loses the zero “UNLESS… you have limit switches and you had honed [homed] your table prior to the program”. My PRO has no limit switches, so after a reinstall, re-find the zero by hand. toolboy, a long-time forum member, t/16514/2: after an error, click the program and choose loop or point. Safety # Never reach under the torch until the CUT45 is switched off. A restart pierces again; keep hands and the fire watch clear. The Run From Here move goes back to the work zero, so check the path for clamps and tip-ups first (guide: check the DRO before Go to Work Zero).
Sources # Langmuir, FireControl guide (pausing; Run From Here; shortcuts; Go to XY Zero): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol-guide Langmuir, FireControl features (Run From Here; Dry Run): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/10840 (staff #2: Run From Line in FC20.5; TinWhisperer #4, #5; strongautoandfab #7, #9) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/14626 (toolboy #2; brownfox #4) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/16514 (toolboy #2) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/30573 (DonP #2, #5; TinWhisperer #3; brownfox #9; ChelanJim #17; OkieBuckeye #18) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31759 (ChelanJim #4; Simsworx #7; A7MOSPHERIC #8) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/37966/4 (ChelanJim) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/28506 (72Pony #2, #4) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12401 (MotoRider42HC #1; jamesdhatch #6) Forum, M00: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/8048/2 (jamesdhatch); https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/13735/1; https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/23300/5 (nicaDd); https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/48685 (ds690 #7; rat196426 #9, #12, #16; poppabear #17, #21)
summary: The torch went out, a consumable failed, or you had to stop part-way through a sheet. When Resume works, when you need Run From Here (loop or line), how to keep the work zero, and why the orange button sometimes does nothing.
title: Scenario: Resuming a Cut After a Stop (Resume, Run From Loop, Run From Line)

Last updated: 30 October 2026
Status: compiled research, not yet tried.
Applies to # My CrossFire PRO with THC, the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) on 230 V, and the X45 machine torch with the machine shield. Mild steel, stainless, and aluminum, mostly 3/16 in and thinner. Doesn’t cover: Hypertherm “cut-quality” guides that depend on Hypertherm cut charts and swirl direction, and the J45XC hand-torch drag technique.
Order to work in (cheapest and most likely first) # Langmuir: “Worn consumables cause most cut-quality problems. Check them before you change any settings.” So:
Consumables. Look at the nozzle orifice (oval, oversized, spatter) and the electrode pit. If in doubt, replace both (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables). Air. 75 psi set during gas check, drains emptied, no water at the cutter (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables). Torch square to the table. Check the torch is vertical in both X and Y with a small square against the torch body and the slats. If it isn’t, follow Langmuir’s Z-axis tram video (5/32 hex and 7/16 wrench). Razorweld: a tilted torch gives “unequal bevel, one side may be excessively bevelled.” Torch height. Razorweld: too high gives “excessive bevel” and a cut that may not go all the way through. Langmuir THC guide: too close gives “more backside dross” and nozzle wear. The target gap is about 0.060 in (THC guide). In SheetCAM that’s a 0.08 in cut height (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height explains why). Make sure THC is on for anything bigger than about 15 x 15 in, or any warped sheet (THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives). Speed. Run the speed ladder from CUT45 cut settings. Heavy bottom dross: too slow. Small hard beads, or spatter on top: too fast. Amps. Thin sheet: lower the amps until the cut is cleanest (Razorweld). 3/16 in: full 45 A and adjust speed. Cut direction (which side gets the bevel). Razorweld: the swirling plasma “bit[es] one side and finish[es] off on the other, leaving a bevelled edge and a straight edge… you want the straight side… on the finished piece.” Test: cut a 2 x 2 in square and a 1 in hole in 3/16 mild. Check the part’s outside edge and the hole edge with a square. If the part edge is the bevelled one, reverse the cut direction for outside profiles in SheetCAM. Make the inside profiles (holes) go the opposite way to the outside profiles. Neither Langmuir nor Razorweld says which direction the X45 swirls, so this test is the only way to know. Material. Stainless and aluminum act differently from mild steel. Razorweld: on aluminum especially, faster tends to be cleaner. Dial in each one separately (CUT45 cut settings). What experienced forum members add # Sources are weighted as described in About this site: Langmuir first, then Razorweld/Jasic, then experienced forum members. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the CUT45.
Measure the real standoff by pausing a cut. ChelanJim (Hypertherm 45XP), t/32789/3. It adds a direct check that the other sources don’t give. Start a long straight cut on scrap. Partway through, press the space bar to pause. Wait for the arc and post-flow to stop. Switch the CUT45 off before reaching under the torch (added here; not in the original post). Slide a feeler gauge under the torch and measure the real gap. Compare it with 0.060 in. ChelanJim found his real height was too high and lowered his post’s cut height from 0.06 to 0.022. That’s his machine and post; don’t copy the number. Measure your own. Bottom dross on straight cuts. Three experienced forum members agree on the usual causes: ChelanJim, t/32789/3: cut height too high, amps too low, or speed too fast. Bigdaddy2166 (Everlast), t/48287/5: torch too high, worn-out consumables, or too slow. Speed and amps are in Razorweld’s and Langmuir’s tables too. Experienced members add torch height, so check it first (pause-and-measure above). Bevel that returns on parts that were clean. ChelanJim, t/32789/3: an enlarged (but still round) nozzle orifice. Swap the electrode and nozzle together. Dross only in small radii and holes. ChelanJim, t/32107/16 and t/32789/3. The machine slows in tight curves, so the cut gets too slow there. Without Fusion’s Feed Optimization, or an equivalent in SheetCAM, he says you get poor hole completion (Kerf width and hole/part accuracy). Cut direction. toolboy (long-time forum member; Everlast), t/28381/41: outside cuts clockwise, inside cuts counter-clockwise, so the good edge is on the part. Check this with a bevel test on your own torch. Measure the actual height. toolboy, t/28381/41: his software setting and his real 0.06 in gap weren’t the same number. Same lesson as ChelanJim’s. Chipping dross off. Wsidr1, t/46239/8: chip it at a shallow angle. Aluminum spatter. Bigdaddy2166, t/36639/3: MIG nozzle anti-spatter gel on the shield. Torch height limit. mechanic416 (long-time forum member), t/20285: 75–80 psi and a height no more than .060 in (already covered above). Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # What you see Likely cause Fix (source) Heavy, bubbly dross stuck on the bottom; arc goes straight down Too slow Raise the feed (Razorweld; Langmuir) Small, hard beads on the bottom; sparks spray up; may not cut through Too fast, or not enough amps Slow down or raise the amps (Razorweld; Langmuir) More dross than usual on a setting that used to work Worn nozzle Replace the nozzle and electrode (Langmuir) More backside dross along with fast nozzle wear Torch too close Check the cut height and THC (THC guide) Bevel on all edges, worse on thicker plate Torch too high, wrong speed, or worn nozzle Height, speed ladder, new nozzle (Razorweld; Langmuir) Bevel on one side only, the same everywhere Torch tilted Square the torch; Z tram video (Razorweld; Langmuir) Bevel on the part side, straight on the scrap side Cut direction reversed for that swirl Reverse the direction in SheetCAM (Razorweld) Bevel that comes and goes on a big sheet Plate warping, height changing THC on; check THC settings (Langmuir) Swirl marks or rough face Moisture in the air Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables (thread 42217) Dross only at the start of each cut Pierce height or delay Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height Community agreement: mechanic416 (thread 20285) lists the same dross causes: too slow, standoff too high, worn parts, wrong amps. He keeps the torch height at or under 0.060 in for cutters up to 60 A.
Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # ChelanJim’s 0.022 in post cut height vs. Langmuir’s 0.060 in gap. ChelanJim’s number was a correction for his own machine reading high; it isn’t a new target. Keep Langmuir’s 0.060 in real gap as the target and use his pause-and-measure method to check it. Cut height: 0.060 vs. 0.080 in. Not a real conflict. 0.060 in is the actual gap (THC guide; mechanic416). SheetCAM’s 0.08 in setting includes IHS springback (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Both are right; use 0.08 in in SheetCAM. Community thin-steel heights of 0.065–0.075 in (community sheet and PWCNC, thread 847; PWCNC’s posts are 847/12, 847/24, and 847/28). It isn’t clear whether these are the real gap or the CAM setting. If they’re the CAM setting, they’re lower than Langmuir’s 0.08. Start at Langmuir’s numbers and test. Safety # See the safety links in CUT45 cut settings. Never cut coated, painted, oily, or galvanized stock without following Langmuir’s safety page and the material’s MSDS.
Sources # Razorweld Razorcut 45 DI manual 2022 (a related but different model, not my JRWPC45LH), “Plasma cutting tips & techniques” (speed, direction, height, tilt): https://razorweld.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/RAZORCUT45DI-INSTRUCTION-MANUAL-2022.pdf Langmuir, consumables and cut problems: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-parts-consumables Langmuir, THC guide (0.060 in gap; too close means more backside dross): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/thc-guide Langmuir, PRO assembly / troubleshooting (Z tram video): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/pro-assembly, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xCbOJz-zfl8 Langmuir, Safety: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/safety Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/20285 (mechanic416), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/847 (thin-steel heights), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/42217 (moisture) Forum, experienced members: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/32789 (ChelanJim: pause and measure; dross causes; bevel), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/32107 (ChelanJim: small radii), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/48287 (Bigdaddy2166: dross), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/28381 (toolboy: cut direction, real height), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/46239 (Wsidr1: dross chipping), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/36639 (Bigdaddy2166: anti-spatter gel) Bernie’s test results # No results logged yet (as of 30 October 2026). Results will come from the test-cut log (result_dross, result_bevel columns) and be listed here with: Date; Material / thickness; Change made; Dross before → after; Bevel before → after; Cut direction that keeps the part square.
summary: Fixing dross and bevel on a CrossFire PRO with the CUT45 and X45 torch, in order from cheapest and most likely: consumables, air, torch square, height, speed, amps, cut direction, material.
title: Getting Rid of Dross and Bevel

content:
Last updated: 30 October 2026
Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads.
Applies to # A CrossFire PRO with THC and IHS and no Limit Switch Kit (my table has none), with programs from SheetCAM 8.0 (Langmuir post). Drawings come from Inkscape or Fusion.
Versions: FireControl 21.1.x and 24.1.6. Set Program Origin and Zero All Axes are on Langmuir’s FireControl features page. No limit switches means there’s no machine home and no soft limits. Langmuir staff say the kit “is what is required to home and use soft / hard limits” (t/19048/2). The homing and soft-limit notes below are only for readers who have the kit. Related: SheetCAM setup and Indexing long parts, which uses Zero All Axes with a shared origin. Check the fixes with a small test file before a real sheet. Symptom (what you’ll see) # The part cuts far from where the torch was zeroed, for example in the middle of the sheet. The part is offset by its own width or height. After a rotate, the origin sits in the middle of the part. A circle doesn’t start where expected. The cut runs off the sheet or into the frame. With the Limit Switch Kit: “Out of range”, “out of bounds”, or “Program Check Encountered an Error”. Likely causes # There are three origins, and the part lands in the wrong place when they don’t line up (per Langmuir staff and experienced forum members). Most likely first:
The SheetCAM origin is in one corner and the part in another. The SheetCAM origin is the corner of SheetCAM’s red sheet rectangle that you chose as the origin. “Wherever you put the part on that red rectangle is where Sheetcam will put it in relation to your chosen table origin” (ds690, t/46038/33). That was TheRock’s six-year mistake, fixed in t/46038/34. The program origin corner doesn’t match the zero corner. The program origin is the point of the drawing that FireControl puts at the work zero. Langmuir: “Change the origin location of your program directly in FireControl” (features page). Click Set Program Origin, and green boxes appear on the corners and the middle of the drawing (ChelanJim, t/34321/2; ds690, t/46038/4). The work zero isn’t where you meant it. The work zero is where the torch is when you press Zero All Axes. ChelanJim: it’s “the location that you plan for your torch to represent the ‘Program Origin’” (t/34321/2). A rotate moved the program origin (ChelanJim, t/33962/28). FireControl’s origin box on circles. ds690 warns that “Firecontrol does weird stuff when the drawing is a circle” (t/46038/4). No soft limits on a PRO without the kit, so nothing stops a program that runs past the sheet (staff, t/19048/2). With the kit, a program past the soft limits gives the Program Check error (PRO troubleshooting; t/31188). Machine home is just where the machine parks. Without limit switches it has no bearing on this (Craig1, t/46038/31).
Fixes (most to least likely) # 1. Place the part the same way at every step # In SheetCAM, put the part at the origin corner. If the origin is bottom-left, move the part so its bottom-left is at or just inside the origin, then post. Do the same in Inkscape or Fusion before exporting (ds690, t/46038/33; Craig1, #31). Load it in FireControl. Fix any errors first (Scenario: a program won’t load). Click Set Program Origin and pick the same corner you’ll zero on. Do it every time, especially after rotating. ChelanJim has had the origin end up in the middle of the part after a rotate, so he always picks it again (t/33962/28). Jog the torch to that corner of the sheet, plus your edge margin, and press Zero All Axes. IHS sets the Z height, so you don’t need to zero Z by hand (Indexing long parts). 2. Check the fit before cutting # Jog the torch around the design’s extents, using the visualizer as a guide, to check it fits on the sheet and inside the travel. ds690 (t/26050/3) and Langmuir staff (t/19048/2) both describe this. Or run a Dry Run (“without Plasma firing and Z-axis moves”; features page). Staff say a Dry Run also checks it, “albeit likely slower” (t/19048/2). 3. Circles # The origin may not line up with the circle’s edge (ds690, t/46038/4). Check a circle’s position by jogging before you cut, and adjust the zero.
4. If you have the Limit Switch Kit (my table doesn’t) # The machine homes to the back-left (upper-left) corner. Most CAD and CAM programs default to a lower-left origin, which is where much of the confusion comes from (ds690, t/31188/2; t/34324). “Out of range” or “out of bounds” with soft limits on usually means the work zero and the program’s position don’t fit inside the soft limits. Re-zero so it fits, and check the soft limits. The troubleshooting page lists G-code past your soft limits as a common cause of “Program Check Encountered an Error”. Break-in program out of bounds: disable soft limits in Machine Settings, run it, then re-enable them (langmuir-reilly, t/30621/4). Typed coordinates: staff’s sequence is Home > set the work coordinates in the DRO > Go to Work Zero (t/26293/2). When that gave a limit error, staff suggested flipping the signs, e.g. (-13, 13) (t/26293/4). Homing in the wrong direction: use Reset Defaults in Machine Settings (PRO troubleshooting). Quick lookup # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Part cuts far from where the torch was zeroed SheetCAM origin in one corner, part in another Move the part to the origin in SheetCAM, then repost (t/46038/31, /33, /34) Part offset by its own width or height Program origin corner doesn’t match the zero corner Set Program Origin to the corner you zeroed (t/34321/2) Origin in the middle of the part after a rotate Rotate moved the program origin Pick the program origin again after a rotate (t/33962/28) Circle doesn’t start where expected FireControl’s origin box on circles Check by jogging; adjust the zero (t/46038/4) Runs off the sheet or into the frame (no limit switches) No soft limits on a PRO without the kit Jog the extents or Dry Run first (staff, t/19048/2) “Out of range” / Program Check error (with the kit) Program past the soft limits Re-zero so it fits; check soft limits (PRO troubleshooting; t/31188) Where sources disagree # Fix it in CAM or in FireControl? TinWhisperer and ds690 say Set Program Origin can fix it without going back to Fusion (t/26050/2; t/46038/4). Craig1 and ds690 (#31, #33) say to fix SheetCAM’s part placement, and that’s what solved t/46038. These aren’t really in conflict. Starting choice: place the part at the SheetCAM origin first, then use Set Program Origin to choose the corner. “Override” or “generate” re-zeroing. Sticks reports that after an override, the generate step may re-zero to wherever the torch is (t/41980/26). No staff confirmation turned up in the research, so treat it as unverified. Check the work zero after any regenerate. What experienced forum members add # ChelanJim, t/34321/5: made annotated screenshots of the FireControl screen explaining these terms. TinWhisperer, t/46038/2: you can’t type in a coordinate to move to (as of Nov 2025). Users have asked for it for years. You jog and Zero All Axes. DKent, t/46038/35: the CAD > SheetCAM > FireControl origin chain is “a topic not well discussed”. That’s why this page exists. Safety # Jogging the extents moves the torch over clamps and tip-ups. Keep hands clear and the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) off while jogging and dry-running. Before Go to XY Zero, check the DRO for a safe path. The button rapids at 300 IPM (FireControl guide).
Sources # Langmuir, FireControl features (Set Program Origin; Dry Run): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol Langmuir, FireControl guide (Go to XY Zero): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol-guide Langmuir, PRO troubleshooting (Program Check error; homing direction): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/protroubleshooting Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/46038 (TinWhisperer #2; ds690 #4, #33; Craig1 #31; TheRock #34; DKent #35) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/34321 (ChelanJim #2, #5) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/26050 (TinWhisperer #2; ds690 #3) Forum, staff: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/19048/2; https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/26293 (#2, #4); https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/30621/4 (langmuir-reilly) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31188/2 (ds690); https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/34324; https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/33962/28 (ChelanJim); https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/41980/26 (Sticks)
summary: The part cuts in the middle of the sheet, off the edge, or FireControl says it’s out of bounds. Last updated: 30 October 2026
Status: compiled research, not yet tried.
Applies to # My CrossFire PRO with IHS standard (a floating-head switch), THC, the SheetCAM FireControl post v1.6, and the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) with the X45 machine torch on 230 V. Doesn’t cover:
The Fusion post’s heights (it adds springback in a different way; see Where sources disagree). Tables without a powered Z. Book pierce delays (including the T45m-format chart reportedly from Jasic, CUT45 cut settings) as final values. FireControl times the pierce delay from the torch-on command, not from arc-on (Langmuir staff quoted by Greg9504, t/12941/2), so book delays run short. Use them as a lower bound. How IHS works with the v1.6 post (so the numbers make sense) # Read straight from FireControl-v1.6.scpost:
Touch off: the torch goes down fast (100 ipm) until the IHS switch trips, then comes back up slowly (20 ipm) until it releases. That’s Z = 0. It goes up another 0.02 in (the “IHS Backlash” move) and calls that Z = 0 again. It rapids to pierce height, fires (M3), and waits for the pierce delay. It moves down to cut height at the plunge rate, then turns the THC on. The touch-off speeds are fixed in the post. The plunge rate only sets the pierce-to-cut-height move. IHS only runs if you set pierce height, plunge rate, and cut height (all non-zero).
The SheetCAM post doesn’t subtract springback (the small amount the floating head moves before the switch trips). That’s why the official SheetCAM tool uses a 0.08 in cut height to get the THC guide’s 0.060 in real gap. That explanation is worked out here from the two posts; Langmuir doesn’t say it directly.
Starting values (Langmuir’s example SheetCAM tool, “Razorcut 45 w/CrossFire PRO”) # SheetCAM field Start value Source Pierce height 0.15 in SheetCAM guide example tool; THC guide (“around 0.15 in”) Pierce delay 0.5 s SheetCAM guide example tool Plunge rate 50 ipm SheetCAM guide example tool Cut height 0.08 in SheetCAM guide example tool Pause at end of cut 0 SheetCAM guide example tool The Razorcut 45 DI manual (a related but different model) says the pilot arc transfers when the torch is 3–5 mm (0.12–0.20 in) from the work; check whether my JRWPC45LH manual gives its own figure. 0.15 in is inside that range.
Corroborated heights. Two sources agree on the real heights: Langmuir, and the T45m-format chart (origin not confirmed):
Cut height, real gap 0.060 in: Langmuir’s THC guide (0.060 in typical), and the T45m-format chart reportedly supplied by Jasic for the CUT45 (torch-to-work 0.06 in on every row, 26 ga to 3/4 in; CUT45 cut settings). Pierce height 0.15 in: Langmuir’s SheetCAM example tool and THC guide, and the T45m-format chart (initial pierce height 0.15 in, 250 % on every row). That chart’s Jasic origin is unconfirmed and its format is Hypertherm’s, so this is supporting evidence, not proven X45 data. Still, 0.060 in real cut gap and 0.15 in pierce height are solid starting points. In SheetCAM the cut height stays 0.08 in: the v1.6 post doesn’t subtract IHS springback, so 0.08 in typed gives about 0.06 in real (see above).
Steps: dialing in pierce and cut height for one material and thickness # Use good consumables and 75 psi (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables), and the amps and speed from CUT45 cut settings. Make a SheetCAM program with ten small separate loops, for example 1 in squares, so you get ten pierces. Run with the starting values. Watch each pierce: Does the arc transfer right away? Does molten metal blow back up at the shield? Does the arc drop out before the torch moves? Look at the shield and nozzle after ten pierces. Spatter stuck to the tip means the pierce is too low or the delay too long for that thickness. Langmuir lists “pierce height that’s too low” as a cause of fast consumable wear. Thin sheet (16 ga and lighter): if the arc goes out or FireControl pauses for lost arc right after the pierce, the delay is too long (THC guide). Shorten it in small steps (for example 0.1 s at a time) and re-test. 3/16 in: if the torch starts moving before the plate is pierced through (a blow-back gouge at the start, or a start that isn’t cut through), lengthen the delay in small steps. If you get “arc lost” right at the start on any thickness, the delay may be shorter than the cutter’s pilot-to-cut time. Lengthen it (THC guide). If the very first pierce of a job misfires but the rest are fine, the post has a setting called firstPierceTime (“an extra delay added to the first pierce as needed by some machines”). It’s 0 by default. Changing it means editing the post file. Keep a copy of the original, and note the change in this page. Cut height: leave it at 0.08 in unless you see the problems in Getting rid of dross and bevel (too high: bevel; too low: backside dross and nozzle wear). Change it in 0.01 in steps and record the THC voltage it gives. Log pierce_height_in, pierce_delay_s, and cut_height_in for every test. What experienced forum members add # Sources are weighted as described in About this site: Langmuir first, then Razorweld/Jasic, then experienced forum members. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the CUT45.
Why book pierce delays run short. Langmuir staff, quoted by Greg9504 (long-time forum member), t/12941/2: FireControl starts the pierce-delay timer at the torch-on command, not when the arc actually transfers. The time the CUT45 takes to fire eats into the delay. So set a little longer than a chart says, and judge by the pierce test (the test-cut program, P1/P2). Check the real height by pausing a cut. ChelanJim, t/32789/3: space bar to pause, arc off, CUT45 off, then feeler gauge under the torch (full steps in Getting rid of dross and bevel). toolboy (long-time forum member), t/28381/41, found the same thing: the software number and the real gap aren’t always equal. Measure once per new setup. SMART locks onto the starting height. 72Pony, t/27956/23: THC samples voltage in the first seconds after IHS. A wrong start height becomes a wrong cut height. Leave Z travel below the zero. ds690 (long-time forum member), t/47251: when the tip touches the metal, there should still be about 1/2–3/4 in of Z travel left. Otherwise Z bottoms out and trips IHS early. Read the generated code if heights look wrong. Blow-back. gamblegarage (long-time forum member), t/236: piercing too-thick plate with the torch too low blows molten metal back into the tip and kills it fast. Don’t lower the pierce height to save time. Plunge rate. nicaDd (long-time forum member), t/21622: at least 50 ipm. This matches Langmuir’s example tool. What a FireControl pierce looks like in G-code. TomWS, t/27189/6, posted this sequence: G38.2 Z-5 F100 G38.4 Z.5 F20 G92 Z0 G0 Z0.15 M3 G4 P0.4 G1 Z0.06 F100 H1 In plain words: probe down, back off until the switch releases, zero Z, rise to the 0.15 pierce height, fire, wait 0.4 s, drop to 0.06 cut height, then THC on. It’s an example from his post, not a value to copy. The v1.6 post’s sequence is in the section above. Heights from experienced members on other cutters (rough only). Bigdaddy2166 (Everlast), t/43254/14, 30 A thin steel: pierce height .12, cut height .062, pierce delay “.05–.07” as written. Bigdaddy2166, t/36639/3, 11 ga aluminum at 40 A: pierce .12–.15, delay .7, cut .06. PWCNC (long-time forum member, 2019), t/847/24 and t/847/28: height about .070 in, delays .9–1.0 s on .105–.120 in steel. Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Arc doesn’t transfer at the pierce Pierce height too high; clamp contact; worn electrode Lower the pierce height toward 0.12 in; clean the clamp spot (THC guide; Razorcut 45 DI manual 3–5 mm; Langmuir consumables) Arc lost right after the pierce on thin sheet Delay too long, so the arc blows a hole and runs out of metal Shorter delay (THC guide) Arc-lost pause right at fire on any thickness Delay shorter than the cutter’s start time Longer delay (THC guide) Blow-back gouge or not pierced through at the start on thicker plate Delay too short Longer delay Spatter welded to the shield or nozzle; parts wear fast Pierce too low Raise the pierce height (Langmuir consumables) Lost arc at the lead-in Lead-in crosses itself or another cut Fix the lead-in (THC guide; SheetCAM 8.0 setup for FireControl) IHS errors or a false trigger before touching No slack in the torch lead pulling the floating head; water at the IHS contact Give the lead slack; dry and grease the contact (Langmuir) Pilot arc held long, then cuts out Pilot over 2 s Check height and transfer (Razorweld) Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # Pierce height 0.12 vs. 0.15 in. Bigdaddy2166 uses .12 on an Everlast. Langmuir and the T45m-format chart both say 0.15. Starting choice: 0.15. Bigdaddy’s number is from a different cutter. Pierce delay timing. Book delays (chart or T45m) assume arc-on timing; FireControl times from the command (t/12941/2). Starting choice: the Razorweld chart’s delays plus some margin, then test. Cut height 0.060 / 0.063 / 0.08 in. THC guide: a 0.060 in typical gap. Fusion post: 0.063 in cut height plus a 0.020 in springback setting. SheetCAM example: 0.08 in. These all agree once you count springback (0.063 + 0.020 is about 0.08). The T45m-format chart (Hypertherm’s Powermax45 format; origin not confirmed) also uses a 0.06 in torch-to-work distance. Starting choice: 0.08 in in SheetCAM (about 0.060 in real), and 0.063 in Fusion’s post as shipped. Plunge rate 50 vs. 100 ipm. The SheetCAM guide’s text says 100; its example tool screenshot says 50. In the v1.6 post, plunge only sets the short pierce-to-cut move. Starting choice: 50 ipm (the CUT45-specific example). Pierce height rule. The Fusion guide says about 2x cut height; the THC guide and SheetCAM example say 0.15 in. These are close (2 x 0.063 = 0.126; 2 x 0.08 = 0.16). The T45m-format chart also uses 0.15 in (250 % of 0.06). Starting choice: 0.15 in. Pierce delay. The Fusion guide says “consult plasma documentation”, but the Razorcut 45 DI manual gives no pierce delay. Community notes from thread 847 include “.001 pierce” and “.3 pierce” for 16 ga and .062 in steel (shorthand; it isn’t clear whether that’s seconds or height). Hypertherm’s T45m delays (0.0–0.9 s by thickness) are for a different torch and run short on Langmuir tables (Greg9504, thread 8193), so they’re a lower bound only. Starting choice: Langmuir’s 0.5 s, or the Razorweld chart’s delay in the test-cut program, then tune by test. Jasic’s posted pierce and cut heights (thread 44500): a search-result summary suggests they’re for Jasic’s own CNC torch, not the X45. That hasn’t been checked against the full thread. Not used. Sources # Langmuir, SheetCAM guide (example “Razorcut 45 w/CrossFire PRO” tool; plunge note): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/software-sheetcam Langmuir, SheetCAM post v1.6 (IHS sequence; firstPierceTime): https://assets.langmuirsystems.com/firecontrol/posts/FireControl-v1.6.scpost Langmuir, THC guide (0.060 in gap; around 0.15 in pierce; lost-arc causes): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/thc-guide Langmuir, Fusion guide (pierce about 2x cut height; consult plasma docs; IHS force): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/software-fusion Langmuir, consumables (pierce too low wears parts): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-parts-consumables Razorweld Razorcut 45 DI manual 2022 (a related but different model, not my JRWPC45LH) (3–5 mm transfer distance; pilot arc over 2 s): https://razorweld.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/RAZORCUT45DI-INSTRUCTION-MANUAL-2022.pdf T45m-format “Torch Setup” chart reportedly supplied by Jasic for the CUT45 (FSFab, https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/45011; origin unconfirmed; Hypertherm format): 0.06 in torch-to-work, 0.15 in pierce height (CUT45 cut settings). Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/8193 (Greg9504: book delays run short), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/847 (community sheet), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/44500 (Jasic chart discussion) Forum, experienced members: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12941 (Greg9504 quoting staff: pierce delay timing), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/32789 (ChelanJim: pause and measure), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/28381 (toolboy), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/27956 (72Pony), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/47251 (ds690: Z travel), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/236 (gamblegarage: blow-back), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/21622 (nicaDd: plunge), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/27189 (TomWS: G-code sequence), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/43254 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/36639 (Bigdaddy2166), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/45011 (FSFab: T45m-format chart) Bernie’s test results # No results logged yet (as of 30 October 2026). Results will come from the test-cut log and be listed here with: Date; Material / thickness; Amps; Pierce ht; Delay; Cut ht; Pierce result (transfer / blow-back / arc lost); Notes.
summary: Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height for a CrossFire PRO with IHS, THC, the SheetCAM FireControl post v1.6, and the CUT45 with the X45 torch: how IHS works, starting values, and a ten-pierce test.

content:
Last updated: 30 October 2026
Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads.
Applies to # A CrossFire PRO with THC and IHS, with programs from SheetCAM 8.0 and the Langmuir FireControl post (Fusion’s Langmuir post also works).
Versions: reports run from FireControl 20.6.2 (2021) to 24.1.6 (2025). The post versions in the files are v1.6 ((v1.6-sc) for SheetCAM, (v1.6-af) for Fusion). Related: SheetCAM setup covers choosing the FireControl-v1.6 post and the (PS…) program-speed line, and how it affects THC. THC setup covers the 85 % speed cutoff. This page is only about files that won’t load. Symptom (what you’ll see) # FireControl rejects a file on the “Validating Program” screen, with one of these:
“No Program Speed Found … will not be loaded” “Program Check Encountered an Error”, sometimes pointing at M30 (the last line) when the file looks fine “Unsupported GCode Command” on a line like DTHC-OFF or M67 FireControl guide: the “‘Validating Program’ screen” means “the USB motion control board is scanning the lines of g-code and checking for any errors”. “If your program has an error, FireControl will let you know the error and the line in the g-code file where the error is present.”
Likely causes # Most likely first:
The wrong or a missing post processor. PRO troubleshooting, “Program Check Encountered an Error”: “Common causes include using the incorrect PostProcessor or uploading a G-code file that surpasses your specified Soft Limits.” “The PS value gets inserted by the post processor” (langmuir-daniel, t/12255/7). Every file from Langmuir’s posts ends with a comment like (PS100). Mach3 programs “will sometimes fail in this way” (langmuirsystems, t/12255/9). A SheetCAM rule writing a code FireControl doesn’t use (“Unsupported GCode Command”; jbrown9709, t/13798/5, /8). The enclosure isn’t connected to the table and switched on (Program Check error at M30). ChelanJim: “FireControl relies on the enclosure to get some of its information when loading a program” (t/42366/15). A file that’s only small circles, where the cut never reaches the tool’s full speed (“No Program Speed Found”; t/42026/10; t/41980/22). A program past the soft limits, if you have limit switches (PRO troubleshooting). A damaged FireControl install, if nothing else explains it. Fixes (most to least likely) # Read the error and line number. FireControl names the line (guide). Open the .tap file in a text editor (Notepad) and go to that line. Check the first line. A file from Langmuir’s v1.6 post starts with (v1.6-sc) (SheetCAM) or (v1.6-af) (Fusion) (ChelanJim, t/42026/8). Anything else (e.g. ( VENDOR AVID CNC)) means it came from the wrong post or machine (TomWS, t/42026/11). Re-post with FireControl-v1.6 (SheetCAM setup). Fusion: pick the post from the setup menu every time unless you’ve saved it as a preference (TinWhisperer, t/19336/2). Tell Fusion where the post file is (ChelanJim, t/42026/6). Check the last line. It should be (PS…) with the program speed, e.g. (PS249) (ChelanJim, t/42026/10; staff, t/12255/9). Missing: wrong post, or a downloaded file that wasn’t posted for FireControl (e.g. a Mach3 file from FireShare) (t/12255/9). Files that are only small circles: ChelanJim relays Sticks’s point that if the cut never reaches the tool’s full speed, you can get this error too (t/42026/10). Sticks reports the same thing with Fusion’s post in t/41980/22. This comes from forum users, not staff. “Unsupported GCode Command” on a line like DTHC-OFF or M67. A SheetCAM rule is writing a code that FireControl doesn’t use. jbrown9709’s came from a tool library he copied from another machine, which brought along a rule (“EOCAnti-Dive … output code: DTHC-OFF”). He fixed it by building his own tool library (t/13798/5, /8). Check SheetCAM’s rules for anything you didn’t add. “Program Check encountered an error” at M30 (the last line) when the file looks fine. Check that the enclosure is connected to the table and switched on. ChadS’s file was fine (ds690 and ChelanJim checked it, t/42366/5, /7). It loaded once the enclosure was back on the table (t/42366/14). My enclosure is wall-mounted by the table, so this mainly matters if the box is ever taken indoors to check files. “Program Check” with limit switches on: re-zero or reposition so the program fits inside the soft limits (Scenario: the part cuts in the wrong place; PRO troubleshooting). Still failing: do a clean FireControl reinstall (steps in Scenario: FireControl won’t open). Then post the G-code and the error on the forum, or send them to support. ChelanJim asks for the G-code text before anything else (t/42366/2). Old files. The downloads page says “Programs posted with older versions of the Post Processors can be converted within FireControl”. Try that before re-posting old jobs. Quick lookup # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) “No Program Speed Found … will not be loaded” Wrong or missing post; no (PS…) line Re-post with FireControl-v1.6; check the last line (t/12255/7, /9; t/19336/2) Same error, file only has small circles Cut never reaches the tool speed See Sticks’s fix in t/42026/10 and t/41980/22 (forum users’ reports) First line isn’t (v1.6-sc) / (v1.6-af) Posted for another machine Select the Langmuir post (t/42026/6, /8, /11) “Unsupported GCode Command” A CAM rule outputs a code FireControl doesn’t support Remove the rule or rebuild the tool library (t/13798/5, /8) “Program check encountered an error … M30” Enclosure not connected to the table Connect the enclosure to the table and switch it on (t/42366/14) “Program Check” with limit switches on Program past the soft limits Re-zero or reposition (Scenario: the part cuts in the wrong place; PRO troubleshooting) Where sources disagree # Delete the bad lines by hand? jbrown9709 first deleted the four M67 lines and the file cut (t/13798/3). The real fix was removing the rule that wrote them (#5). Starting choice: fix it in CAM. Hand-edited files get overwritten the next time you post. Reinstall vs. connect the enclosure (t/42366). ChelanJim suggested a reinstall (#7). It didn’t help, and connecting the table did (#14). For an M30 Program Check error, check the connections first. What experienced forum members add # ChelanJim, t/42366/7: H0 is in every program’s opening lines so the controller takes charge of Z for the IHS sequence. ChelanJim says this comes from Langmuir. Don’t strip it out. ds690, t/42366/5: M30 at the end is normal, and the (PS60) line is the program speed. Wsidr1, t/42366/16: suggests a small enclosure simulator would let people check files indoors. There isn’t one; plan to load files at the table. Safety # A file from the wrong post can contain moves or Z commands the PRO isn’t set up for. Never “fix” a file by deleting lines you don’t understand and then cut with it. Re-post it, then Dry Run with the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) off (SheetCAM setup).
Sources # Langmuir, FireControl guide (Validating Program; error line): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol-guide Langmuir, PRO troubleshooting (Program Check Encountered an Error): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/protroubleshooting Langmuir, downloads (post processors; converting older programs): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/downloads Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12255 (3,574 views; langmuir-daniel #7; langmuirsystems #9) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/19336/2 (TinWhisperer) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/42026 (ChelanJim #6, #8, #10; TomWS #11) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/13798 (solved; jbrown9709 #3, #5, #8) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/42366 (solved; ChelanJim #2, #7, #15; ds690 #5; ChadS #14; Wsidr1 #16) Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/41980/22 (Sticks, Fusion post and circles)
summary: FireControl rejects a file while it’s validating it. On the forum the cause is nearly always the post processor, a CAM rule that writes a code FireControl doesn’t know, or loading with the table disconnected. How to read the file’s first and last lines to tell which.
