content:
Last updated: 30 October 2026
Status: compiled research, not yet tried.
Applies to # My CrossFire PRO (rated accuracy 0.002 in per 12 in, step resolution 0.0005 in, ACME lead screws with anti-backlash nuts) with THC. The Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) is on 230 V with the X45 machine torch, and I make kerf offsets in SheetCAM v8 with the FireControl v1.6 post. Doesn’t cover: XR ball-screw accuracy figures, Hypertherm kerf tables, and Fusion’s kerf compensation (I use SheetCAM).
Status: The only Langmuir kerf number for this cutter is 0.06 in, in the example SheetCAM tool. Community numbers range from 0.021 in to 0.059 in. Measure your own for each amps, speed, and thickness combination.
Steps: measuring kerf # Dial in amps, speed, and heights first (CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings and Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Kerf changes with every one of them. In SheetCAM, make a tool with kerf width = 0. Draw a 2.000 x 2.000 in square. Cut it as an outside profile with no offset (“on the line”), with the lead-in in scrap. Let it cool, knock off the dross, and measure the square across the flats in X and in Y with calipers, top and bottom faces (bevel makes them differ). Kerf = 2.000 − measured size. The torch took half a kerf off each side. Use the average of X and Y, top side, for the SheetCAM kerf width. Write down the bottom-side number too. Put the measured kerf in that SheetCAM tool and in the log (kerf_set_in, kerf_measured_in). Check it: cut the same 2.000 in square as an outside-offset part, plus a 1.000 in hole as an inside offset. Measure both. If the square is undersize and the hole oversize, the kerf setting is too small; increase it by the error. If it’s the other way around, reduce it. Steps: hole test coupon # On a 6 x 4 in coupon of the material, draw holes of 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 3/4 and 1 in, plus a 2 in outer square. Use inside offsets for the holes and an outside offset for the outer edge. Lead-ins: start each hole near its center with a short straight or arc lead-in that doesn’t cross itself. No lead-out (Langmuir; see THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives). Cut order: holes first, outside last, so the part doesn’t move before the holes are cut. Check the cut-order setting in the SheetCAM plasma operation (the v8 default hasn’t been confirmed here), and step through the preview to confirm the order. THC on small holes: with Langmuir’s defaults, THC doesn’t act on loops shorter than 0.5 in, and it freezes whenever the feed is under 85 % of the program’s fastest feed (THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives). You don’t need to turn THC off by hand for holes. Feed rate for holes: No Langmuir or Razorweld rule for slowing down on small holes turned up in the research. Run the coupon at the line-cut speed first. If holes come out tapered, out of round, or with a divot where the cut finishes, try a second coupon with the hole operation slower (separate SheetCAM operation). Record both. Measure each hole top and bottom with calipers or pin gauges. Write down the smallest hole that comes out round and usable for each thickness. Rule of thumb: if a hole has to be accurate, cut it undersize and drill or ream it to size. What experienced forum members add # Sources are weighted as described in About this site: Langmuir first, then Razorweld/Jasic, then experienced forum members. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the CUT45.
Estimate kerf from the tip. 72Pony (CUT60), t/28035/10 and t/12723/18. Rule of thumb: kerf ≈ orifice + 0.01 in. For my X45’s 1.0 mm (0.040 in) tip (mechanic416, t/21266), that’s about 0.050 in. mechanic416 (long-time forum member) says the X45 tip’s kerf is at least 0.055 in. Langmuir’s example tool uses 0.06. So expect 0.050–0.060 in, and measure. 72Pony’s measuring method. Draw a 2 in square with a 1 in hole. Cut it on the line (no kerf offset). Measure the square. Drawn size minus measured size = kerf. For example, 2.000 in drawn and 1.945 in measured means kerf = 0.055 in. Kerf grows as the tip wears, so re-check with a new tip. Commissioning squares. TomWS, t/24586/2: 2 in square: IHS dry run with plasma off, THC off cut, THC on cut, then measure and adjust kerf. ChelanJim, t/41575/4: a 2 in box with a 3/4 in circle; and a kerf of 0 is always wrong. Holla2040 (same CUT45), t/35995/10: cut about 30 test squares with 1 in circles to dial his in. SheetCAM’s kerf only shifts the path. toolboy (long-time forum member), t/24105/2. The real kerf comes from the nozzle, amps, speed, and air. The setting just tells SheetCAM how far to offset. Pierce and lead-in placement. richarddbeck83 (Everlast), t/39953/6: the pierce offset must be bigger than the kerf, so the pierce lands in scrap. Use a lead-in angle under 90°, and pierce at the largest part of the feature. jamesdhatch (long-time forum member), t/19097/2: lead-in about 2x kerf. A shorter one leaves a divot. Wsidr1, t/46239/8: pierce inside the circle (the scrap), not on the line. Gaps between parts. Wsidr1, t/34970/9: at least 2x kerf. Small holes. ChelanJim, t/32789/3: without Feed Optimization (Fusion) or an equivalent, expect poor hole completion. SheetCAM’s matching setting hasn’t been identified yet (SheetCAM 8.0 setup for FireControl). TomWS, t/36785/19, and toolboy, t/35951/14: for accurate holes, mark them (peck or center-punch) with the plasma and drill them. Thin-sheet kerf numbers from other setups (rough only). PWCNC (long-time forum member, torch not confirmed): .021–.026 in at 28 A on .062 steel (t/847/12); .040 in at 35 A on .120 steel (t/847/28). Cletus (CUT60): .025 in at 31 A on 16 ga aluminum, 150 ipm (t/18698/46); and .025 in at 30 A on 16 ga steel, 150 ipm (t/20256/7). These are two different posts on different metals, checked against both posts on 30 October 2026. Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) All parts undersize and holes oversize by the same amount Kerf set too small Raise the SheetCAM kerf by the error Kerf wider than before at the same settings Worn nozzle or low air pressure New nozzle; check the regulator (Langmuir) Kerf wide on thin sheet Too many amps Lower the amps (Razorweld) Holes tapered (bigger on top) Bevel: height, speed, nozzle Getting rid of dross and bevel Divot or notch where the hole closes Lead-out, or the arc lingering at the end No lead-out; try a slower hole feed; check pause at end = 0 Holes oval in one direction Lost steps or play in X or Y; a loose coupler Squaring the gantry and fixing lost steps (coupler Sharpie test; carriage preload) Parts wrong size along a long dimension Machine accuracy limit, or not square Langmuir rates 0.002 in / 12 in; Squaring the gantry and fixing lost steps Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # Expected X45 kerf. 72Pony’s rule gives about 0.050 in; mechanic416 says at least 0.055 in; Langmuir’s example tool uses 0.06 in. These are close. Starting choice: 0.06 in in SheetCAM, replaced by the measured number (72Pony’s method) for each amps setting.
Kerf numbers.
Langmuir example tool: 0.06 in. Thread 31041 (general forum member): 0.045–0.059 in at 45 A. Cletus, thread 20256 (post 7): 0.025 in, 16 ga steel, 30 A, 150 ipm. (His 31 A figure in t/18698/46 is for 16 ga aluminum.) Thread 847 community sheet: 0.021–0.026 in for 0.062 in steel at 28 A. These can all be right because kerf shrinks with lower amps and faster speed. Starting choices: 0.06 in at 45 A on 3/16 in, and Cletus’s 0.025 in at 30 A on 16 ga steel, then replace both with your own measurement.
Small-hole feed reduction. No source turned up in the research. Don’t use any percentage until it’s tested.
Sources # Langmuir, SheetCAM guide (example tool kerf 0.06 in): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/software-sheetcam Langmuir, CrossFire PRO page and product page (accuracy, resolution): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-pro, https://www.langmuirsystems.com/products/crossfire-pro-cnc-plasma-table Langmuir, THC guide (SMART distance; CUTOFF %): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/thc-guide Langmuir, Fusion guide (no lead-out with THC): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/software-fusion Langmuir, consumables and cut problems (wide kerf): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-parts-consumables Langmuir, SheetCAM post v1.6 (program speed): https://assets.langmuirsystems.com/firecontrol/posts/FireControl-v1.6.scpost Razorweld Razorcut 45 DI manual 2022 (a related but different model, not my JRWPC45LH) (kerf and amps): https://razorweld.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/RAZORCUT45DI-INSTRUCTION-MANUAL-2022.pdf SheetCAM plasma manual: https://www.sheetcam.com/Download/SheetCam%20TNG%20Plasma%20Manual_A4.pdf Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/20256 (Cletus), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31041, https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/847 Forum, experienced members: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/28035 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12723 (72Pony: kerf), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/21266 (mechanic416: X45 tip, kerf ≥ 0.055), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/24586 (TomWS), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/41575 (ChelanJim), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/35995 (Holla2040), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/24105 (toolboy), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/39953 (richarddbeck83), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/19097 (jamesdhatch: lead-in), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/46239 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/34970 (Wsidr1), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/32789 (ChelanJim: holes), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/36785 (TomWS: drill holes), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/35951 (toolboy), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/847 (PWCNC 847/12, 847/28), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/18698 (Cletus) Bernie’s test results # No results logged yet (as of 30 October 2026). Results will come from the test-cut log and be listed here with: Date; Material / thickness; Amps / feed; Kerf measured (top / bottom); 1 in hole measured; Smallest usable hole; Notes.

Applies to # SheetCAM 8.0 on Windows, making G-code for FireControl on my CrossFire PRO with IHS and THC, using Langmuir’s FireControl-v1.6.scpost. Designs come from Inkscape (SVG or DXF) and Fusion (DXF). Doesn’t cover:
The Mach3/Legacy SheetCAM posts. Langmuir’s “CrossFire without Z-axis” tool example, which has pierce and cut height set to 0. That would turn off IHS. The Fusion post’s own settings, if you post from Fusion instead. Note: Langmuir’s SheetCAM guide was written for an older SheetCAM and still shows post V1.1 in its screenshots. Menu names in SheetCAM 8.0 may differ slightly. Look for the same settings by name.
Steps: one-time setup # Download the post. Get the latest FireControl – SheetCAM Post from Langmuir’s Downloads page. As of this writing it’s FireControl-v1.6.scpost. Langmuir: the latest firmware needs the latest posts. Install it. Copy the file into SheetCAM’s Posts folder. Langmuir says it’s usually C:\Program Files (x86)\SheetCam TNG\Posts, but check on your own computer. SheetCAM 8.0 may use a different folder; confirm and write it here: ______. Options → Machine: Machine type: Jet Cutting on, Rotary Cutting off. Post processor: choose FireControl-v1.6 (not V1.1 as shown in the guide pictures). Output units and output folder: your choice. Keep units the same as your FireControl setting. Z zero: Top of Work. Make one plasma (jet) tool per material, thickness, and amps. Put the amps in the name, for example “MS 3/16 45A”, because FireControl doesn’t set amps (Langmuir staff, thread 5883). Start values from Langmuir’s example “Razorcut 45 w/CrossFire PRO” tool: Field Start value Replace with Kerf width 0.06 in Your measured kerf (Kerf width and hole/part accuracy) Feed rate (blank in example) Your speed-ladder winner (CUT45 cut settings) Pierce delay 0.5 s Your tested delay (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height) Pierce height 0.15 in Your tested value (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height) Plunge rate 50 ipm Leave it Cut height 0.08 in Your tested value (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height) Pause at end of cut 0 Leave it IHS only runs if pierce height, plunge rate, and cut height are all set (post file header). Never set them to 0 on the PRO.
Lead-in / lead-out defaults: Lead-in: a short lead-in that doesn’t cross itself or another cut (THC guide: self-intersecting leads lose the arc). Lead-out: none (Langmuir Fusion guide for PRO + THC: “use NO lead out”; same reason applies in SheetCAM). Put lead-ins on the scrap side: outside of parts, inside of holes. Save as defaults / save the tools so every new job starts with them. Steps: every job # Import the DXF or SVG (File → Import drawing). Check the scale straight away: measure one known dimension in SheetCAM. Inkscape SVGs sometimes come in at the wrong scale if document units and import units don’t match. Add a plasma operation with the right tool. Holes get an inside offset, the part outline an outside offset, and engraving lines no offset. Cut order: holes and inside features first, outline last. Step through the preview to check. Cut direction: set it so the straight side of the cut is on the part (Getting rid of dross and bevel test). Mixed speeds in one file: the post writes the fastest non-lead-in feed in the file as program speed (the (PS…) line at the end). The THC freezes below 85 % of that (default Torch Speed CUTOFF). A slower hole operation will run with THC frozen automatically (THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives). Post the code. Open the .tap/.nc file in a text editor once to check: the first line must read (v1.6-sc) (thread 27030). If it doesn’t, SheetCAM isn’t using the v1.6 post. In FireControl: load the program, zero X and Y, and run Dry Run (no plasma, no Z moves) to check the path stays on the sheet. Then cut. Note for the future: arcs smaller than 0.05 in come out as straight segments in this post, which is fine for plasma. What experienced forum members add # Sources are weighted as described in About this site: Langmuir first, then Razorweld/Jasic, then experienced forum members. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH).
Back up the SheetCAM settings folder. TomWS, t/2424/59. It’s at C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Roaming\SheetCam TNG. Copy it, don’t move it. Do this before changing the post or tools. What actually reaches FireControl. ChelanJim, t/1146/14 and t/31750/2. With the Fusion post, only the cut speed and kerf go into the G-code. Amps and air are set on the cutter. Langmuir staff say the same for SheetCAM (amps aren’t set by FireControl, t/5883). Put the amps in the tool name. Lead-ins. jamesdhatch (long-time forum member), t/19097/2: about 2x kerf. With a 0.06 in kerf, that’s roughly 0.12 in. richarddbeck83, t/39953/6: pierce offset bigger than the kerf; lead-in angle under 90°; pierce at the largest part of the feature. Open lines vs. closed shapes. Wsidr1, t/34970/9: Use a separate operation with center (no offset) compensation for open lines. Keep gaps between parts at least 2x kerf. Cut direction. toolboy (long-time forum member), t/28381/41: outside cuts clockwise, inside counter-clockwise. Marking holes for drilling. toolboy, t/35951/14: use a drilling-type operation to mark holes, then drill them. Plunge rate. nicaDd, t/21622: at least 50 ipm. Small holes. ChelanJim says Fusion’s Feed Optimization matters for hole quality (t/32789/3). SheetCAM’s matching option hasn’t been identified yet; it isn’t covered in the Langmuir sources used here. Holla2040 (same cutter), t/31460: spent hours on 18 ga SheetCAM settings, and made his own Fusion post changes. His changes aren’t covered here; this page sticks to the stock v1.6 post. Inkscape. jamesdhatch, t/12525/1: stroke settings when exporting (see Langmuir’s Inkscape guidance). Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) FireControl won’t run the file or shows a program error Not a Langmuir post, or an old post Re-post with FireControl-v1.6 (FireControl guide) First line isn’t (v1.6-sc) Wrong or old post selected; more than one copy installed Remove old posts, clean-reinstall v1.6, re-select it in Options → Machine (thread 27030, DannyD) No IHS before cuts Pierce height, plunge rate, or cut height is 0 Set all three (post header) Program bigger than the table or soft-limit alarm Wrong units or scale on import Check scale (step 1) and output units Arc lost at the lead-in Lead-in crosses itself or another cut Redraw the lead-in (THC guide) Torch dips at the end of each cut Lead-out on Set lead-out to none (Fusion guide) THC never engages on any of the job One fast operation sets the program speed and everything else is under 85 % Split into separate files, or lower CUTOFF % (THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives) Torch rises 1 in after every cut Normal; hard-coded in the post Nothing to fix (SheetCAM guide) Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # Plunge rate. SheetCAM guide text: 100 ipm. Example tool: 50 ipm. In v1.6 the IHS speeds are hard-coded (fast down 100, slow up 20), and plunge only sets the short pierce-to-cut move. Starting choice: 50. Cut height on thin gauge. Langmuir’s guide says to add extra cut height on thin gauge because of springback, without a number. The example tool’s 0.08 in already includes about 0.02 in (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Raise it only if a test cut on thin sheet shows the torch too close. Pierce and cut heights. The guide says “consult your plasma cutter manufacturer”. Razorweld doesn’t publish them for the X45. Starting choice: Langmuir’s example values. Sources # Langmuir, SheetCAM guide: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/software-sheetcam Langmuir, Downloads (latest posts): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/downloads Langmuir, SheetCAM post v1.6: https://assets.langmuirsystems.com/firecontrol/posts/FireControl-v1.6.scpost Langmuir, FireControl guide (approved posts only; Dry Run): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/firecontrol-guide Langmuir, Fusion guide (no lead-out with THC): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/software-fusion Langmuir, THC guide (lead-in self-intersection): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/thc-guide SheetCAM plasma manual: https://www.sheetcam.com/Download/SheetCam%20TNG%20Plasma%20Manual_A4.pdf Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/27030 ((v1.6-sc) check; DannyD reinstall), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/5883 (amps not set in FireControl), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12670 (update FireControl / post v1.6); not yet read for this site: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/6321, https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/17006 Forum, experienced members: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/2424 (TomWS: settings folder), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/1146 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31750 (ChelanJim: what reaches G-code), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/19097 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12525 (jamesdhatch), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/39953 (richarddbeck83), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/34970 (Wsidr1), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/28381 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/35951 (toolboy), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/21622 (nicaDd), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/32789 (ChelanJim), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/31460 (Holla2040) Bernie’s test results # No results logged yet (as of 30 October 2026). Results will be added here as they come in, with: Tool name; Material / thickness; Amps; Feed; Kerf; Pierce ht / delay; Cut ht; Proven on (date).

Status: compiled research, not yet tried.
Applies to # My CrossFire PRO: dual Y lead screws and a single X lead screw (ACME; Langmuir’s comparison page lists 3/8 in-8 4-start Y with a 1/2 in 5-start X, while current PRO pages say 1/2 in 5-start on all axes. Measure yours; the procedures are the same either way), acetal anti-backlash lead nuts, NEMA 23 steppers, couplers (2-screw aluminum or 4-screw steel), and V-groove bearing carriages with adjustable bearing blocks. No limit switches unless I add the kit. The PRO has no belts, so belt-tension advice doesn’t apply. Also doesn’t cover:
The XR’s ball screws, pulleys, and set-screw notes (thread 21584 is XR). The original CrossFire/XL gantry video. The MC4000 electronics. Steps: checking for square # Put the Marker Pen Attachment (or a sharp pointer) in the torch mount. Draw a large rectangle, as big as the table comfortably allows (for example 30 x 30 in), on a flat sheet or on paper taped to a sheet. Program it in SheetCAM and run it following Langmuir’s Marker Pen instructions. Dry Run mode doesn’t fire the plasma. Measure both diagonals with a good steel tape, hooked on the same side of the line each time. If they’re equal, the gantry is square. If they differ by more than you can measure reliably, re-square. Also measure the sides. If X and Y sides are both off by a similar percentage, that’s a scale problem (lost steps or slipping couplers), not a square problem. Langmuir staff (thread 9412) also recommend a test square as the check.
Steps: squaring the gantry (Langmuir PRO assembly, final steps 6–7) # Power on the electronics so the motors hold. Connect FireControl. Loosen the lead nuts: the 2 bolts on the X lead nut, the 2 bolts holding the X lead-nut tab to the X carriage, and the 4 bolts on each Y lead nut. Loosen until the nuts can float. In FireControl, jog to maximum +X (right arrow) and minimum −Y (down arrow). When the gantry is close to the stanchion plates, set the jog speed to 50 ipm. Tap −Y repeatedly until the bearings on both gantry carriages lightly touch the stanchion plates. That squares the gantry to the slat bed. Tighten in this order: the 2 bolts on the X lead nut, then the 2 bolts on the X lead-nut tab, then the 4 bolts on each Y lead nut. Re-check with the diagonal test above. Staff alternative (thread 9412, Langmuir staff; summarized from search results, not checked against the full thread, so read it before using this): loosen the Y coupler(s), turn the Y lead screw by hand until that side seats against the stanchions, then re-tighten the couplers using the procedure below, with the motors powered.
Steps: coupler tightening (Langmuir PRO assembly step 6, with motors powered) # Tighten the inside screws snug. Tighten the outside screws snug. Turn the inside screws another 1/8–1/4 turn. Turn the outside screws another 1/8–1/4 turn. Grab the lead screw and try to turn it against the motor. If the coupler slips, repeat steps 3–4. Caution (Langmuir): too much torque can strip the screws or the hex key.
Steps: when a motor stalls or the table loses position (Langmuir PRO troubleshooting) # Work through these in order:
Coupler slip test. Put three Sharpie dots in a line: one on the coupler, one on the motor shaft, one on the lead screw. Jog back and forth. If the dots separate, re-tighten the coupler (above). Y carriage realignment (PRO only). Redo PRO assembly Step 5. On each of the 8 adjustable bearing blocks, seat both cap screws, then back them off about 1/4 turn. Turn the adjustment set screw clockwise until at least one opposing fixed bearing touches the rail and no play can be felt. Then tighten the cap screws. Dry lead screw. Lubricate with machine oil and jog the full travel so it gets into the lead nuts. Don’t use white lithium grease, WD-40, or dry lube on the lead screws (Langmuir). Wrong bearing mount. The X motor and bearing mounts are shorter than the Y ones. Both Y mounts should be the same length. Mounts out of square bend the lead screw slightly. Check them with a protractor or square. Bent lead screw. Take it out and roll it on a flat, clean surface. Langmuir says to straighten a slight bend by hand. Lead nut installed wrong. Compress the anti-backlash spring fully while threading the nut onto the screw. Lead nut tab out of square (rare). Loosen its 4 bolts, jog, and see if the binding goes away. Motor plug arc damage or a loose plug. This is the usual cause if a motor sometimes jogs the wrong way. With power off, unplug each motor’s D-sub and look for burning, melting, or charring. Re-plug it and tighten both D-sub screws, with no wiggle. Z axis. If Z sticks or has play, adjust the eccentric bearing axles with a 5 mm wrench: clockwise adds preload. Use the minimum preload that removes play while Z still slides freely. Clean the Z rails with solvent, and check the torch is square with the Z tram video. After any rebuild, run Langmuir’s PRO break-in program (CrossFire PRO-BreakIn-v1.6.tap). If you have the Limit Switch Kit, soft limits may need disabling because the break-in program runs the full travel (Langmuir). What experienced forum members add # Sources are weighted as described in About this site: Langmuir first, then Razorweld/Jasic, then experienced forum members. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH).
If the frame itself is out of square. toolboy (long-time forum member), t/26365/27. When adjusting the gantry couldn’t fix it, he: Took the gantry off. Loosened the frame bolts. Squared the frame by measuring corner to corner (both diagonals equal), keeping it level. Tightened the frame, then refit the gantry. It’s a big job. Do it only if the diagonal check on this page shows the frame is the problem. Follow Langmuir’s assembly steps when refitting. Recheck before the final tightening. 72Pony, t/45654/4: follow Langmuir’s squaring directions exactly, and recheck square before the final tightening. Lost steps that are really noise. Bigdaddy2166, t/48104/10: EMI ground straps on the motors. Work through Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise first. Z bottoming out. ds690 (long-time forum member), t/47251: leave about 1/2–3/4 in of Z travel when the tip touches the metal (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom Likely cause Fix (source) Diagonals unequal; parts are parallelograms Gantry out of square Squaring steps (PRO assembly step 7) Parts shift partway through a job, same axis each time Coupler slipping Sharpie test; re-tighten (PRO troubleshooting) Motor buzzes or stalls in one spot Binding: dry screw, bent screw, mount out of square, lead nut Langmuir PRO troubleshooting guide, stalling and binding sections A–F Stalls only at high speed Binding plus speed; machine max is 300 ipm Fix the binding; lower the feed or rapid speed for that job Motor sometimes runs the wrong way Arc-damaged or loose D-sub motor plug Inspect, re-seat, screw down (Langmuir PRO troubleshooting guide, section G) Holes oval along one axis Play in carriage bearings or coupler Carriage preload Step 5; coupler test Torch hits tipped-up parts and the table loses position Collision Clear the slats; the IHS auto-lifts 1/16 in on contact (PRO assembly), but a hard hit can still shift the gantry. Re-zero Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # How tight to make couplers. PRO assembly: snug plus 1/8–1/4 turn, with a stripping warning. PRO troubleshooting: tighten “until they cannot be tightened any more” if they slip. Start with the assembly procedure, and only go tighter if the Sharpie test still shows slip, stopping before anything strips. Lubrication. Langmuir says no WD-40 on the lead screws, but it does say to use WD-40 on the sidewall of a sticky Z bearing (troubleshooting). These are different parts, so both apply. Squaring method. The assembly guide (jog against the stanchions with nuts loose) and staff thread 9412 (seat against the stanchions by turning a Y screw) agree on the principle. Starting choice: the assembly guide. Sources # Langmuir, PRO assembly (Step 5 carriage preload; final steps 6 couplers and 7 squaring; Z table): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/pro-assembly Langmuir, PRO troubleshooting (stalling and binding A–G; break-in and soft limits; Z preload): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/protroubleshooting Langmuir, coupler tightening video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tftc32RcxT8 Langmuir, Z-axis tram video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xCbOJz-zfl8 Langmuir, PRO break-in program: https://assets.langmuirsystems.com/file/CrossFire+PRO-BreakIn-v1.6.tap Langmuir, CrossFire PRO specs (lead screws, 300 ipm, accuracy): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-pro Langmuir, Limit Switch Kit: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/products/limit-switch-kit-for-crossfire-and-crossfire-pro Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/9412 (staff squaring), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/21584 (XR only, not used) FireShare, “Crossfire Pro Index and squaring gauge” (community): https://fireshare.langmuirsystems.com/projects/crossfire-pro-index-and-squaring-gauge-3150 Forum, experienced members: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/26365 (toolboy: frame re-square), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/45654 (72Pony: recheck square), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/48104 (Bigdaddy2166: EMI straps), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/47251 (ds690: Z travel) Bernie’s test results # No results logged yet (as of 30 October 2026). Results will be added here as they come in, with: Date; Rectangle size; Diagonal 1; Diagonal 2; Side X / side Y; Action taken; Notes.

Last updated: 30 October 2026
Status: planned; no results logged yet (as of 30 October 2026).
Applies to # My CrossFire PRO with IHS and THC, the Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) on 230 V, and the X45 machine torch with the 51206 tip, cutting mild steel, stainless, and aluminum. The goal is to turn the Razorweld-supplied chart (Razorweld to MO-Hacker, CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings) into my own chart, checked on my machine, with every cut logged in the test-cut log. Plan settings come from the Razorweld chart, Langmuir’s defaults, and Razorweld’s manual. The second candidate, the T45m-format chart reportedly supplied by Jasic (FSFab, t/45011; origin unconfirmed), supplies the T2 voltage and an optional 45 A comparison session (CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings). No number in this plan is a tested result until it’s been cut and logged. Doesn’t cover: Powermax or other cutters’ test charts, or XR/belt-machine calibration.
One material and thickness per session: 10 coupons plus one or two short test lines, about one shop afternoon. Don’t mix thicknesses in a session; you won’t know what changed.
The test coupon (draw it once, reuse it forever) # Draw this once in Inkscape or Fusion and save it as test-coupon.dxf. Origin is the bottom-left corner of the rectangle.
Feature Size and position What it tells me Outer rectangle 3.000 x 2.000 in Kerf (two directions), dross, bevel, edge square Large hole 1.000 in diameter, center at (0.900, 1.000) Hole size and roundness, bevel on holes Small hole 0.500 in diameter, center at (2.250, 1.000) Small-hole quality (THC usually off on these) Straight line 4.000 in open cut, from (−0.500, −0.750) to (3.500, −0.750) Clean drop line to read lag lines, dross, and slot width The footprint is about 4 x 3 in. Space coupons 5 in apart in X and 4 in apart in Y. Ten coupons (two rows of five) fit on a piece about 26 x 9 in. The H1/H2 test lines need their own strip, about 12 x 3 in. Use flat, clean scrap; for thin sheet, weight or clamp it flat.
SheetCAM, once (SheetCAM 8.0 setup for FireControl for the post and tool setup):
Import test-coupon.dxf. Check the scale: the rectangle must measure 3.000 x 2.000.
Operations, in cut order:
Both holes: inside offset, lead-in from the center. The line: no offset (on the line). The rectangle: outside offset. Lead-ins in scrap and no lead-outs (THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives; SheetCAM 8.0 setup for FireControl). Check the order in the preview.
Make a test tool: kerf width 0 (so I can measure kerf), pierce height 0.15 in, pierce delay per the session table, plunge 50 ipm, cut height 0.08 in (Langmuir guide; Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Put the amps in the tool name, for example TEST MS16 25A.
Post one program per coupon, changing only what that coupon tests. Name each file with the session and coupon, for example S01-L1-091.tap. Open each file and check that the first line reads (v1.6-sc) (SheetCAM 8.0 setup for FireControl).
At the table: jog to the next empty spot, Zero X and Y (keep Z as FireControl sets it with IHS), and run the next file.
Prep, every session (about 15 minutes) # Drain the compressor tank and the filter bowls (Razorweld manuals, including the JRWPC45LT sister manual: drain the tank daily). Dry-air check: after the drain, the bowls should stay dry through the session. Write “bowls dry: yes/no” in the notes of the first log row. Water means fix the air first (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables). Fresh consumables: new electrode and tip together, assembled in the torch diagram’s order (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables). Write 0 in consumables_pierce_count on coupon 1 and count up one per pierce. Each coupon has 4 pierces: 2 holes, 1 line, 1 rectangle. 75 psi at the cutter during the gas test (CUT45 gas check button; Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables). Write the psi you actually saw. Set the amps on the CUT45 knob to the session amps. FireControl doesn’t set amps (thread 5883). Clean ground to the work: clean the work-clamp spot and check continuity from the clamp to the test piece (Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise). Grounding of the cutter and house wiring: follow my CUT45 manual and an electrician, not this page. Square and tram check: torch vertical in X and Y with a small square (Langmuir Z tram video; Getting rid of dross and bevel). Gantry check from Squaring the gantry and fixing lost steps if it’s been a while. THC settings at Langmuir defaults (SMART voltage, 85 % cutoff, 5 % Z-speed; THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives). Safety: eye protection to ANSI Z87.1 / Z49.1, ventilation, and fire watch (Langmuir safety page; my CUT45 manual). Never cut coated or galvanized test scrap; follow the manufacturers on fumes. The coupons in a session (in this order) # # Coupon What changes Everything else 1–5 L1–L5 speed ladder Feed: chart optimum −20 %, −10 %, 0, +10 %, +20 % Chart amps; ladder pierce delay; THC on, SMART voltage (0). Write the Live Volts reading for each. — Pick a provisional winner Grade L1–L5 and choose the best feed The winner’s Live Volts is the SMART voltage for the 3-way test 6 H1 height-reference line (line only) THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives’s manual-nominal test: THC off, Z motor unplugged, torch set to a real 0.060 in gap with a feeler gauge; read Live Volts Provisional feed; no IHS loop. This is my torch’s measured voltage at 0.060 in (6b) H2 second height line (optional, line only) The same, at a real 0.120 in gap Lets me turn any voltage into an estimated torch height (below) 7 T1 THC fixed at the Razorweld chart’s voltage Nominal Voltage = Razorweld chart arc V for this thickness (152 V for S01, 147 V for S04) Provisional feed; ladder delay 8 T2 THC fixed at the Jasic/T45m chart’s voltage Nominal Voltage = T45m chart voltage for this thickness (session table; for example 118 V for 3/16 mild; 111 V for 16 ga mild at that chart’s 30 A, or 116 V at its 45 A). The T45m amps differ from my session amps. Provisional feed; ladder delay 9 P1 pierce delay Delay one step shorter than the ladder Provisional feed; the THC choice that won the 3-way test 10 P2 pierce delay Delay one step longer (on 25 A rows: no delay, 0 s) Same 11 V1 verification Kerf width = my measured kerf Winning feed, delay, and THC choice The THC test comes before the pierce-delay tests on purpose. Voltage sets the real torch height, and height affects both the pierce and the edge, so the height gets settled first. The speed ladders are the same as before.
Speed limit: never post a rung above 300 ipm (PRO max). If the +20 % rung is over 300, cut it at 300 and say so in the notes.
Pierce delay steps use the delays that appear in the Razorweld chart: 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 s. The chart gives no delay for its 25 A rows, so those ladders use 0.5 s (Langmuir’s SheetCAM guide example), and P1/P2 test 0.25 s and 0 s.
Session table (planned settings, from the Razorweld chart on the cut settings page; T2 from the T45m-format chart) # Session Material Thickness Amps Chart arc V (T1) T2 V (T45m row used) Ladder pierce delay (s) Chart optimum L1 −20 % L2 −10 % L3 0 L4 +10 % L5 +20 % S01 Mild steel 16 ga 25 A 152 111 (16 ga, 30 A; 116 at 45 A) — (use 0.5) 114 91 103 114 125 137 S02 Mild steel 14 ga 40 A 144 117 (14 ga, 45 A) 0.25 221 177 199 221 243 265 S03 Mild steel 10 ga 40 A 146 117 (10 ga, 45 A) 0.50 98 78 88 98 108 118 S04 Mild steel 3/16 in 40 A 147 118 (3/16, 45 A) 0.75 63 50 57 63 69 76 S05 Stainless 16 ga 40 A 144 116 (16 ga, 45 A; 111 at 30 A) 0.25 243 194 219 243 267 292 S06 Stainless 14 ga 40 A 144 117 (14 ga, 45 A) 0.25 144 115 130 144 158 173 S07 Stainless 10 ga 40 A 147 117 (10 ga, 45 A) 0.50 70 56 63 70 77 84 S08 Stainless 3/16 in 40 A 149 118 (3/16, 45 A) 0.75 44 35 40 44 48 53 S09 Aluminum 1/16 in 25 A 152 118 (16 ga, 30 A) — (use 0.5) 174 139 157 174 191 209 S10 Aluminum 1/8 in 40 A 149 122 (10 ga 0.135, 45 A; nearest row) 0.50 133 106 120 133 146 160 S11 Aluminum 3/16 in 40 A none 123 (3/16, 45 A) 1.00 none 38 49 59 71 85 T2 note: the T45m chart has only 30 A and 45 A rows. For 25 A sessions, use its 30 A row; for 40 A sessions, its 45 A row. The amps don’t match exactly, so T2 is a ballpark, not a like-for-like setting. The T45m chart has no 1/8 in aluminum row; S10 uses the nearest (10 ga, 0.135 in). S09 (aluminum 1/16 in) stands in for “16 ga” in aluminum; the Razorweld chart lists aluminum in fractions, not gauges. S11 (aluminum 3/16 in) has no chart row. Its ladder isn’t ±20 %. It starts at 38 ipm (the Razorcut 45 DI manual’s 5 mm figure, a related model), then 49 ipm (the Razorweld chart’s 1/4 in row, which 3/16 should at least match), then +20 % steps (59, 71, 85). Delay starts at 1.00 s (the 1/4 in row), with P1/P2 at 0.75 and 0.50 s. Amps 40 A, the same as the chart’s 1/8 and 1/4 rows. Mild 14 ga uses the 221 optimum; ignore the chart’s odd 640 max (CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings, oddities). 11 ga isn’t in the chart. If it’s stocked later, give it its own session later, starting from a ladder that covers both neighbors. Steps: running a session # Do the prep list above.
Cut L1 to L5 in order, slowest first. Watch the arc under the plate through proper lenses. Razorweld: the arc should trail “at a slight angle away from the direction of travel”; straight down is too slow; sparks spraying up on top is too fast. Read Live Volts in FireControl partway along the line cut and write it in that row’s notes as liveV=___.
Let the coupons cool. Knock them out and grade each one (judging guide below). Pick the provisional winner: the rung with the least dross that’s easy to remove, the squarest edge, and a clean line cut. If two tie, take the faster one. If the winner is L1 or L5 (an end of the ladder), the best may be beyond it. Note it, and run another ladder past that end next session.
3-way THC voltage test at the provisional feed and the ladder delay. The three candidates are:
SMART: the winner’s Live Volts from step 2. That rung is already cut; no new coupon. The Razorweld chart’s voltage: T1. The Jasic/T45m chart’s voltage for this thickness: T2 (session table). The sub-steps:
H1 first (THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives’s manual-nominal steps). Gauge the torch to a real 0.060 in gap; don’t use SheetCAM’s 0.08 here, because there’s no IHS springback in this test (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Turn the electronics box off, unplug the Z motor, power up, cut an 8–10 in line, and read Live Volts. Write it in thc_voltage on the H1 row. If you can, start the line at the plate edge rather than piercing at 0.060 in, which is hard on the tip; the T45m-format chart uses edge starts on thick plate. See firecontrol/fc-01-straight-cut-edge-start.md for edge-start methods. H2 (optional): repeat at a real 0.120 in gap. With the electronics box off, plug the Z motor back in, power up, and check that IHS works on a scrap touch-off before going on. Cut T1, then T2, each with the THC on and Nominal Voltage set. Stand by the pause/E-stop. If the torch dives into the plate, climbs away, or loses the arc, stop, set Nominal back to 0, and write what happened. A stopped coupon is a valid result. Measure the real torch height. FireControl’s Z readout won’t show THC moves (THC guide), so read height from voltage. Arc voltage rises as the torch goes up and drops as it gets closer (THC guide). A voltage near H1 means about 0.060 in. Higher means higher; lower means lower. With H2 too, estimate: height ≈ 0.060 + (V − H1) × 0.060 ÷ (H2 − H1). That’s a straight-line approximation worked out for this plan, not a Langmuir formula. Use it for SMART, T1, and T2. Better, direct check: pause and measure (ChelanJim, t/32789/3; Getting rid of dross and bevel). On a long straight line, press the space bar partway through, wait for the arc and post-flow to stop, switch the CUT45 off, and slide a feeler gauge under the torch. Write it as gap=___ in the notes. Do this at least on the SMART winner, T1, and T2. Watch the THC up/down LEDs at the start of each cut. A long run of one direction means the THC is driving the torch away from the 0.060 in it started at. Measure bevel on the rectangle of the SMART winner, T1, and T2. Put a small square against each long edge, and write square, slight, heavy, or one-side in result_bevel. A torch running too high shows bevel on all edges (Getting rid of dross and bevel). Also note the slot width of the line. Pick the THC choice. It’s the best edge (dross, then bevel) of the three. SMART (0) stays the default unless T1 or T2 is clearly better (Langmuir staff recommend SMART; thread 5883). Write down whether the Razorweld chart’s voltage (139–152 V range) or the T45m chart’s (111–123 V) lands closer to H1 on my torch. That answers CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings’s voltage conflict. Cut P1 and P2 at the provisional feed with the winning THC choice. Look at the start of each cut. Too short: a blow-back gouge, or not pierced through at the start. Too long: on thin sheet the arc blows a hole and is lost right after the pierce (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height). Keep the shortest delay that pierces cleanly every time. The T45m chart’s delays are shorter than the Razorweld chart’s. FireControl times the delay from the torch-on command, not arc-on (staff quoted by Greg9504, t/12941/2), so book delays run short. Treat the T45m delays only as a floor. If a delay shorter than the T45m value looks clean, repeat it on a second coupon before trusting it.
Measure kerf on the winning coupon (method below). Set that kerf in the tool and cut V1. Measure V1’s rectangle and holes, and write the error from nominal in the notes.
Fill in all rows in the CSV. Copy the winner into CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings’s “Bernie’s test results” table.
Optional session S04B: 45 A T45m settings vs. the Razorweld chart (3/16 mild steel) # Why: FSFab (t/45011) says the T45m-format 3/16 settings fixed “pierces, then torch goes out” on his CUT45 machine torch. This session checks whether they beat the Razorweld chart’s 40 A settings on my machine. Run it after S04, on the same batch of 3/16 plate, with consumables that still look good.
# Coupon Amps (knob) Feed Pierce delay THC Source J1 Razorweld chart baseline 40 A 63 ipm (or the S04 winner) 0.75 s (or the S04 winner) SMART (0) Razorweld chart; S04 result J2 T45m settings, delay with margin 45 A 85 ipm 0.75 s (0.5 book + 0.25 margin for FireControl’s start delay; a margin chosen for this plan, not a measured number) SMART (0) T45m 3/16 row; t/12941/2 J3 T45m settings, book delay 45 A 85 ipm 0.5 s SMART (0) T45m 3/16 row J4 T45m settings, fixed voltage 45 A 85 ipm the better of J2/J3 Nominal 118 V T45m 3/16 row Steps:
Cut J1 at 40 A. Turn the CUT45 knob to 45 A before J2. Write the amps in every row. Cut J2, J3, J4. Use the pause-and-measure check on J2 and J4 (gap=___). Grade all four with the judging guide. Measure kerf on J1 and J2 (it’s likely wider at 45 A). Duty cycle: 45 A on 3/16 is hard on the cutter (25 % in the Razorcut 45 DI manual; 30 % in JRWPC45LH listings; check my manual). Let it rest between coupons. If the overheat light (or an E60/E61 code) comes on, leave the machine on and wait (CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings). Verdict: if J2 or J3 is clearly cleaner than J1, run a short 45 A ladder (68, 77, 85, 94, 102 ipm) next time before adopting it. Otherwise keep the Razorweld chart’s 40 A settings. Kerf measurement (coupons cut with kerf width 0) # Use calipers on the top side, away from the lead-in. Write bottom-side numbers in the notes if they differ.
Rectangle: measure X (nominal 3.000) and Y (nominal 2.000). Cut on the line with kerf 0, the part comes out undersize by one kerf width. Kerf = ((3.000 − X) + (2.000 − Y)) ÷ 2. Holes: with kerf 0 they come out oversize by about one kerf. The 1.000 hole minus 1.000 should roughly match the rectangle number. It’s a cross-check. Line: the slot width in the middle of the line (caliper inside jaws) is a direct, rough kerf reading. Put the rectangle number in kerf_measured_in. Kerf width and hole/part accuracy has the full method. Judging guide # Look at Good Too slow Too fast Other causes Bottom dross None, or a thin line that falls off Heavy, bubbly globs that knock off easily (low-speed dross) Small, hard beads rolled onto the bottom edge, hard to remove (high-speed dross) Worn tip; wrong height (files 04, 06) Top spatter Clean top edge — Sparks spraying up during the cut; spatter on top Pierce too low or delay too short at the start only (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height) Bevel (square against the edge) Square, or about the same on both sides Can widen Can increase Torch tilted (one side, everywhere); torch too high (all edges); cut direction reversed (part side only) (Getting rid of dross and bevel) Lag lines (drag lines on the cut face) Fairly straight down the face Nearly vertical, with heavy dross Curving strongly backward against the travel, often with beads — Line cut Cut through end to end — Not cut through in spots Amps too low Source notes:
Dross types: Langmuir’s consumables page (slow = heavy dross on the bottom, fast = small beads) and Razorweld’s tips. Arc angle: Razorweld. Lag-line reading: general plasma-shop practice. Neither Langmuir nor Razorweld describes it, so treat it as a supporting clue, not the deciding one. How to write results in the log (keep the words the same every time so it can be sorted):
result_dross: none, light, heavy-bubbly, hard-beads, or not-through. result_bevel: square, slight, heavy, or one-side, plus which side in the notes. What to record in test-cut-log.csv, one row per coupon # Column What to write date Cut date, YYYY-MM-DD material mild_steel, stainless, or aluminum thickness_in Actual thickness, calipered if you can (16 ga steel is nominally 0.0598) amps Knob setting psi What the gauge showed during the gas test feed_ipm Feed used for that coupon pierce_height_in, pierce_delay_s, cut_height_in As set in the SheetCAM tool. On H1/H2: the real gauged gap (0.060 or 0.120) in cut_height_in, with pierce fields blank thc_on yes or no thc_voltage 0 for SMART, the number for a fixed nominal (T1, T2), or the Live Volts reading on H1/H2 kerf_set_in 0 on test coupons; your measured kerf on V1 kerf_measured_in Kerf from the rectangle formula consumables_pierce_count Running pierce total on this electrode and tip at the end of this coupon result_dross, result_bevel Words from the judging guide notes liveV=___, bowls dry yes/no, hole sizes, anything odd. No commas; use semicolons source_setting Where the setting came from, for example chart opt 114 -20% or Langmuir example 0.5s session_id For example S01-MS-16GA The log already has planned rows for S01 (mild steel 16 ga), S04 (mild steel 3/16 in), and the optional S04B. Results are blank, so fill them in as you go. For the H, T, P, and V rows, write the provisional winning feed into feed_ipm once it’s known. Write each estimated height in the notes as height~___.
Deciding the winner and updating the chart notes # The winner is the coupon with the cleanest dross, then the squarest bevel, then the fastest feed. If the winner is within one rung of the chart optimum, the Razorweld chart is confirmed for that row. Write “confirmed” in CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings’s results table. If the winner is at L1 or L5, the Razorweld chart is off for that row. Run another ladder beyond it before calling it. Write the winning amps, feed, pierce delay, THC choice, and measured kerf into CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings’s results table. Then make a SheetCAM tool for it (SheetCAM 8.0 setup for FireControl). Re-check a winner after any change of consumable brand, air setup, or cutter, or after a big crash or rebuild. Symptoms -> causes -> fixes (during testing) # Symptom Likely cause Fix Every rung has heavy dross Wrong amps, worn tip, or height too high New consumables; check the height (Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height); try one ladder at 45 A on thick stock (Razorweld rule; CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings) Every rung has hard beads or isn’t cut through Feed too high for the amps Run a lower ladder starting at L1’s speed Results get worse coupon by coupon Tip wearing, or water arriving Look at the tip; check the bowls (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables) Torch dives or climbs on T1 or T2 That voltage doesn’t match a sensible height on my torch Back to SMART (0); that’s a valid result. Compare with H1 H1 voltage far from all three candidates Gap not really 0.060, or worn tip Re-gauge with the Z motor unplugged; check the tip (Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables) Holes oval or undersized on one side Gantry or coupler issue, not cutting Squaring the gantry and fixing lost steps Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # Ladder center: the Razorweld chart’s optimum (Razorweld to MO-Hacker; weighted with the Razorweld manual, below Langmuir) over the T45m/Jasic chart and other forum numbers (CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings). The manual’s figures are the sanity check. The T45m chart gets its own test in T2 and S04B. Pierce delay on 25 A rows: the chart gives none. Start from Langmuir’s 0.5 s example and test shorter. Fixed voltage vs. SMART: Langmuir staff favor SMART. The Razorweld chart’s voltages (139–152 V) have no height attached. The T45m/Jasic chart gives 111–123 V at a stated 0.06 in, but its origin is unconfirmed (CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings). SMART stays the default unless T1 or T2 proves better. H1 is my torch’s own measured voltage at 0.060 in, and that beats both charts. Order of tests: the THC test now comes right after the ladder, before the pierce tests, so the pierce tests run at the height that will actually be used. The ladder runs on SMART because that’s the default. Pierce delays: the Razorweld chart’s steps are the plan. The T45m chart’s shorter delays are a lower bound only, because FireControl times from the torch-on command (t/12941/2). Sources # Razorweld-supplied chart (Razorweld to MO-Hacker, https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/847/29; its settings have worked well for me, not formally tested): CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings. Razorweld Razorcut 45 DI manual 2022 (a related but different model, not my JRWPC45LH) (gas check, tank draining, arc-angle speed check, thick vs. thin amps, Table 7.1.3, safety): https://razorweld.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/RAZORCUT45DI-INSTRUCTION-MANUAL-2022.pdf Langmuir, consumables and cut problems (dross types): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-parts-consumables Langmuir, THC guide (SMART voltage, defaults, manual nominal test): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/thc-guide Langmuir, SheetCAM guide (example tool: pierce 0.15 in, delay 0.5 s, cut height 0.08 in): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/software-sheetcam Langmuir, CrossFire PRO (300 ipm): https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/crossfire-pro Langmuir, Safety: https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/safety Langmuir, Z-axis tram video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xCbOJz-zfl8 T45m-format chart reportedly supplied by Jasic for the CUT45 (FSFab, https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/45011; Jasic origin unconfirmed; Hypertherm format): T2 voltages and session S04B, CUT45 (X45 torch) cut settings. Forum: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/5883 (staff: amps not set by FireControl; SMART voltage), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/8193 and https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/12941 (Greg9504 quoting staff: pierce delay timed from the torch-on command), https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/32789 (ChelanJim: pause and measure) Bernie’s test results # No results logged yet (as of 30 October 2026). The table below lists the planned sessions; it gets one summary row per session, with details in the test-cut log (test-cut-log.csv).
Session Date Material / thickness Winner feed Delay SMART V H1 V (0.060 in) THC choice Kerf Chart confirmed? Notes S01 Mild steel 16 ga S04 Mild steel 3/16 in
summary: A planned, coupon-by-coupon test program for checking the Razorweld-supplied chart (and the T45m-format chart’s voltages) on a CrossFire PRO with the CUT45 and X45 torch, with every cut logged.
title: Test-Cut Program: Checking the Starting Settings, Coupon by Coupon

content:
Last updated: 30 October 2026
Status: compiled research, not yet tried.
Applies to # Written for my setup: a CrossFire PRO with 48 in (X) x 33 in (Y) cut area, ACME lead screws, IHS standard, Langmuir THC installed, no Limit Switch Kit unless I add one. Torch is the Razorweld X45 machine torch in the Machine Torch Mount, on a Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) running on 230 V. Langmuir says a full 4 x 8 sheet can pass through the PRO front to back, so a long part has to lie along Y. The PRO can’t be expanded to 4 x 8. Doesn’t cover: the XR has 48 x 96 travel and needs no indexing. The PRO MAX (48 x 48) and the original CrossFire/XL have different travel limits. The Mach3 indexing write-ups are for Gen1 legacy machines.
I couldn’t find an official Langmuir indexing or tiling procedure (as of October 2026). The steps below combine Langmuir’s own features (zeroing, Dry Run, Go to XY Zero, the Marker Pen) with community methods. Try the method on scrap first.
Before you start # Check that the gantry is square (see Squaring the gantry and fixing lost steps). Any racking error shows up twice when you index. Have adjustable-height stands ready. Langmuir recommends them for any sheet hanging off the table. A full sheet is heavy and the edges are sharp. Use gloves and get help lifting. Steps # Orient the part. In Fusion or Inkscape, turn the part so its long side runs along Y (front to back). Pick the split line(s). Each segment has to fit inside the 33 in Y travel with room to spare. Community examples: segments laid out to fit a 32 x 48 window (JPep, thread 20780) and 30 in segments (Brian344, same thread). Put each split across a straight section of the part, not on a curve or a small feature. Split the drawing into separate programs that share one origin. Program A holds everything from Y = 0 up to the split line. Program B holds the rest, moved by exactly the index distance D toward −Y (for example, 30.000 in). Use the same X zero and the same coordinate system (JPep, 20780). JPep breaks the profile at the split with a 0.001 in gap so each program gets an open path that ends right at the split. Don’t overlap the lines. A double-cut leaves a notch. Put lead-ins in scrap, not at the split. Leave out lead-outs on the THC table (see THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives). Set a fence along Y. Clamp a straight bar on the slats, parallel to Y travel, for the sheet’s left edge to ride against. To check it’s parallel, put the Marker Pen (or a pointer) in the torch mount and jog the full Y travel along the fence. The gap shouldn’t change. Set a stop for the index distance. Clamp a stop block on the fence, or make two scribe marks D apart on the sheet. Mark them both on the sheet and on a fixed point of the table. Zero the machine. Jog to your corner and use ZERO ALL AXES. IHS sets Z, so don’t zero Z by hand. Write down the DRO position of a physical reference: tape a scrap of tape on the frame and line up a mark on it. Dry run Program A. FireControl Dry Run mode runs with no plasma and no Z moves. Watch for anything running off the sheet or hitting a clamp. Cut Program A. Don’t move the gantry zero. With the torch parked up and out of the way, slide the sheet by exactly D toward −Y, so the line that was at Y = D now sits at Y = 0. Check which physical direction −Y is on your table by jogging first. Keep it against the fence until it hits the stop or the marks line up. Check the alignment before cutting. Load Program B and use “Go to XY Zero”. Jog the marker or pointer to one end of the cut from Program A and confirm it lands on the cut. Brian344 (20780) dry-runs with a pointer before each segment. If it’s off in Y, re-slide the sheet. Re-zeroing to make up for a bad slide works, but then your reference is the cut, not the fence. Dry run Program B, then cut it. Measure the joint. Look for a step (an X error) and a gap or overlap (a Y error). Write it in the test-cut log. Symptoms -> causes -> fixes # Symptom at the split Likely cause Fix Step sideways (X) Sheet moved off the fence, or fence not parallel to Y Re-check the fence with the marker (step 4). Clamp the sheet lightly to the fence while sliding. Gap or overlap along Y Index distance D wrong, or the stop moved Measure D with a steel rule or tape, re-set the stop, and check with “Go to XY Zero” before cutting. Segments meet at an angle Gantry out of square, or the sheet rotated while sliding Square the gantry (Squaring the gantry and fixing lost steps). Use two fence contact points. Notch or double-burn at the join The two programs overlap at the split Break the path at the split (0.001 in gap, JPep). Keep lead-ins away from the split. Lost position after a pause Gantry was jogged, or the zero was overwritten Re-find the cut from Program A with the pointer and re-zero there. Use Run From Here for the rest. What experienced forum members add # Sources are weighted as described in About this site: Langmuir first, then Razorweld/Jasic, then experienced forum members. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the CUT45.
Indexing pin vs. scribe line (t/21633#2). The idea (DRotblatt, long-time forum member): put a 1/8 in pin about 0.25 in in from the X25/Y0 corner as a stop. Have Program A cut a 0.125 in index hole in the sheet. Slide the sheet, drop the hole over the pin, then run Program B. TomWS (experienced forum member) replied that he doubts a plasma-cut index hole is any more accurate than lining up a scribe line. Suggested starting point: use the scribe line or stop block plus the pointer check (steps 5 and 10). Treat the pin as an experiment; if you try it, measure the joint (step 12) and compare. TinWhisperer points to his video for cutting images larger than the table (t/46165). The thread has no written steps; watch the video before trying anything different. No Langmuir staff advice on indexing turned up in the research. Where sources disagree (and the starting choice) # Index pin vs. scribe line (t/21633). A plasma-cut pin hole has kerf and dross, so it’s only as good as the cut. TomWS doubts it beats a scribe line. Starting choice: follow TomWS (scribe line or stop, plus the pointer check). Re-zero after sliding vs. not re-zeroing. A community method (threads 20200, 8748, 13570) is to slide against blocks and run the second program without re-zeroing. Brian344 (20780) checks each segment with a pointer. Starting choice: combine them. Keep the zero (fewer places to make a mistake) and check with the pointer before firing. These are general forum posters; no Langmuir staff or frequently cited members posted on this in the threads found. Work offsets. FireControl has stored work coordinates, but homing and work offsets need the Limit Switch Kit, which isn’t standard on the PRO. Without the kit, don’t count on returning to a stored offset after a power cycle. Results will come from the test-cut log and be listed here with: Date; Material / thickness; Index distance D; X step at join; Y gap/overlap; Method used; Notes.

Last updated: 30 October 2026
About this site # These are my personal notes (Bernie Lindsey). I’ve run my CrossFire PRO since August 2024. I put them together with help from an AI research assistant that read Langmuir and Razorweld documents and Langmuir forum posts. Where a page says “I” or “my”, it means me and my machine: a CrossFire PRO with THC, a Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH) on 230 V with the X45 machine torch, and a wall-mounted electronics enclosure, in a home shop. The full list is under “My setup” on the home page.
The site is unlisted: it isn’t in search engines, but anyone with the link can read it. I’m sharing it in case it helps other CrossFire owners.
What’s tested and what isn’t # Most of this site is compiled research that I haven’t tried yet. The settings from the forum-posted Razorweld chart have worked well for me, and I’ve used the scrap lead-in edge start (FC-01 Method 1) a few times. Nothing here has been formally tested yet. The test-cut program is how I plan to do that.
Each page starts with a status line:
Tested on my machine: cut and logged in the test-cut log. Nothing has reached this yet. Used by me, not formally tested: I’ve done it and it worked, but there are no measured results. Compiled research, not yet tried: collected from the sources listed on the page. Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads: the FireControl scenario pages (FC-02 to FC-07). They collect common problems forum members run into, with the fixes the forum and Langmuir settled on. They’re for looking things up, not steps I’ve run. Planned: the test-cut program, worksheet and log. No results are logged yet. Where a page says “Starting choice”, “my starting choice” or “suggested starting point”, that’s the setting I plan to start from, not a result.
How sources are weighted # Langmuir’s own documents and staff. Razorweld/Jasic manuals and manufacturer-supplied charts. My own printed JRWPC45LH manual comes first. The online Razorcut 45 DI manual is for a related but different model, so its figures are only a guide until checked against mine. Experienced forum members whose posts are cited often here (for example TomWS/TinWhisperer, ChelanJim, Bigdaddy2166, richarddbeck83, 72Pony, Cletus, Wsidr1, Holla2040). Other long-time forum members. Everyone else. Every number on the site says where it came from. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the CUT45. Forum members are quoted from public posts, with links. The forum citations were gathered with the research assistant, and not every quote has been checked against the full thread, so read the linked post before relying on it.
Not official # I’m not affiliated with Langmuir Systems, Razorweld, or Jasic. Always follow the manufacturers’ manuals, safety instructions, and support advice over anything here. Settings are starting points, not proven values. Corrections are welcome on the Langmuir forum.
Glossary # CUT45 (JRWPC45LH): my cutter, the Razorweld CUT45 CNC, model JRWPC45LH, built by Jasic. Langmuir sells it as the “Razorweld Razorcut 45 with Machine Torch”. Earlier versions of this site called it the “Razorcut 45” or “Razorweld 45”. The Razorcut 45 DI is a related but different Razorweld model with its own manual. THC (torch height control): Langmuir’s add-on that reads the arc voltage during a cut and moves Z to keep the torch at a steady height. Arc voltage / Live Volts: the voltage across the arc while cutting. Higher voltage means a higher torch. The CUT45’s divider port sends it to the THC divided by 50 (the “50:1” port). SMART voltage: the THC setting (Nominal Voltage = 0) that reads the arc voltage right after IHS and holds it for the rest of that cut loop. Langmuir staff recommend it. IHS (initial height sensing): the PRO touches the torch to the plate before each pierce to find the surface, then lifts to the pierce height. It uses a floating-head switch. Pierce height / pierce delay: how high the torch sits while the arc first burns through the plate, and how long it waits there before moving. Cut height vs. real gap: the cut height typed into SheetCAM (0.08 in) is larger than the actual gap under the torch (about 0.060 in), because the floating head springs back after IHS. See Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height. Kerf: the width of the cut slot. CAM offsets the toolpath by half of it so parts come out the right size. Dross / bevel: dross is the re-solidified metal stuck to the bottom edge; bevel is an edge that isn’t square. Razorweld chart: the CUT45 cut chart Razorweld sent to forum member MO-Hacker (t/847/29). It’s my starting chart. Its Optimum column is the suggested feed; Max is the fastest that will still sever the metal. T45m-format chart: a CUT45 chart that forum member FSFab says Jasic supplied (t/45011). Its layout and its “T45m shielded consumables” label match Hypertherm’s Powermax45 charts (T45m is Hypertherm’s Powermax45 machine torch), so its origin is unconfirmed. Post processor (“post”), v1.6: the SheetCAM or Fusion file that turns toolpaths into G-code FireControl understands. Langmuir’s current one is v1.6. Test sessions S01–S11: one session per material and thickness in the test-cut program. For example S01 = 16 ga mild steel and S04 = 3/16 in mild steel. S04B is an optional extra session on 3/16 in mild steel that compares the T45m-format chart’s 45 A settings with the Razorweld chart’s 40 A settings. Coupon codes within a session: L1–L5 = a speed ladder (chart feed −20 % to +20 %); H1/H2 = height-reference lines for reading voltage at a known gap; T1/T2 = THC fixed at the Razorweld or T45m-format chart’s voltage; P1/P2 = pierce-delay checks; V1 = a final verification coupon with the measured kerf. Forum links like t/847/29: thread 847, post 29 on forum.langmuirsystems.com.

My setup # Table: Langmuir CrossFire PRO, 48 x 33 in cut area, ACME lead screws, IHS standard, Langmuir THC added. Electronics on 120 V, in an enclosure wall-mounted away from the table. Cutter: Razorweld CUT45 CNC (model JRWPC45LH; Langmuir sells it as the “Razorweld Razorcut 45 with Machine Torch”) on 230 V (20–45 A), X45 machine torch in the Machine Torch Mount. Air: Ingersoll-Rand SS3L3 60-gallon compressor → IR D18IN refrigerated dryer → Harbor Freight filter → cutter. Software: Inkscape and Fusion (design), SheetCAM 8.0 with the FireControl post v1.6 (CAM), FireControl (machine control). Materials: mild steel, stainless, and aluminum, mostly 3/16 in and thinner. Shop: a home shop. My setup: the CUT45 and the Ingersoll-Rand dryer and compressor, the wall-mounted electronics enclosure, and the CrossFire PRO with the X45 torch. Tap to enlarge. How to read these pages # Status line. Every procedure page starts with one of: Tested on my machine (nothing yet), Used by me, not formally tested, or Compiled research, not yet tried. The FireControl scenario pages (FC-02 to FC-07) are marked Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads, and the test-cut pages are marked planned. How sources are weighted: Langmuir’s own documents and staff first, then the Razorweld/Jasic manuals (my printed JRWPC45LH manual first; the online Razorcut 45 DI manual is for a related but different model), then experienced forum members, then everyone else. Every number says where it came from. Numbers from members with a different plasma cutter are only a rough guide for the CUT45. Cut charts. I couldn’t find a published X45 machine-torch cut chart (as of October 2026). My starting chart came from Razorweld: they sent it to forum member MO-Hacker, who posted it (https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/847/29). Because it’s manufacturer data, it’s weighted just below Langmuir’s own documents. I’ve cut with these settings and they worked well, but they haven’t been formally tested yet. A second candidate is a T45m-format chart (laid out like Hypertherm’s Powermax45 charts; T45m is Hypertherm’s Powermax45 machine torch) that FSFab says Jasic supplied (https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/45011; origin unconfirmed). Its arc voltages (111–123 V) disagree with the Razorweld chart’s (139–152 V). The test-cut program is how I plan to settle that. Safety items (house wiring, grounding the supply, fumes from coated or galvanized stock) go to the manufacturers’ documents. See https://www.langmuirsystems.com/pages/safety and the printed operating manual that came with my cutter (JRWPC45LH). Test results go in the test-cut log. It has planned rows for test sessions S01 (16 ga mild steel), S04 (3/16 in mild steel), and the optional S04B (3/16 in mild steel, T45m-format chart at 45 A vs. Razorweld chart at 40 A). Results then go into each page’s “Bernie’s test results” section. Site map # About this site: who wrote this, what’s tested, how sources are weighted, and a glossary. Charts: the Razorweld chart and the T45m-format charts as images. The typed-in tables are on the cut settings page. Test-cut log: the planned and logged coupons, with a CSV download. Sources: every forum and official link. Procedures # THC setup, tuning, and stopping torch dives Work clamp, grounding, and electrical noise Air supply, air quality, and X45 consumables CUT45 cut settings: starting points and dialing in. Razorweld-supplied chart first; T45m-format chart reportedly from Jasic as a second candidate (the voltage conflict is spelled out). Getting rid of dross and bevel Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height Kerf width and hole/part accuracy SheetCAM 8.0 setup for FireControl Squaring the gantry and fixing lost steps Test-cut program: checking the starting settings, with a printable worksheet. The order is: a speed ladder, then a 3-way THC voltage test (SMART voltage vs. the Razorweld chart’s voltage vs. the T45m-format chart’s voltage), then pierce delays. An optional session (S04B) compares the two charts head to head on 3/16 in mild steel. Indexing parts longer than the table. Compiled research, kept for reference and listed last, since my parts fit within the PRO’s roughly 33 in of Y travel. FireControl # FC-01: Straight Cut starting at the plate edge. Method 1 (a scrap lead-in piece) is the one I’ve used, a few times; not formally tested. Methods 2 and 3 are collected from forum posts and haven’t been tried. FC-02: Scenario: FireControl won’t open (“Child process exited with code 1”). The most-viewed FireControl problem on the forum. Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads. FC-03: Scenario: FireControl won’t connect: CrossFire greyed out, or only a COM port shows. Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads. FC-04: Scenario: connection lost or frozen mid-cut, computer side. Check EMI in grounding first. Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads. FC-05: Scenario: resuming a cut after a stop: Resume, Run From Loop or Line, and M00 pauses. Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads. FC-06: Scenario: the part cuts in the wrong place: work zero, Set Program Origin, and the SheetCAM origin. Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads. FC-07: Scenario: a program won’t load: No Program Speed Found, Program Check error, Unsupported GCode. Reference: compiled from Langmuir docs and forum threads. Quick-start values (Langmuir SheetCAM guide example tool for a Razorweld 45A cutter on the PRO; test before trusting) # Pierce height 0.15 in · pierce delay 0.5 s · plunge 50 ipm · cut height 0.08 in in SheetCAM (about 0.060 in real; heights also match the T45m-format chart reportedly from Jasic, see Pierce height, pierce delay, and cut height) · kerf 0.06 in · air 75 psi · THC defaults (SMART voltage, 85 % cutoff, 5 % Z-speed).
Feed rate and amps: start from the Razorweld chart’s Optimum column (CUT45 cut settings), then check them with the test-cut program’s speed ladder.
Questions I plan to ask Langmuir or Razorweld support (no answers yet) # On a PRO with the stainless water table, where should the work clamp go now: frame, drain plug, slat bed, or workpiece? (Langmuir’s documents give different locations.) Can Razorweld confirm the chart it gave MO-Hacker (t/847/29) is for the X45 machine torch, and which arc voltages are right? Is there an official X45 machine-torch cut chart: amps, speed, kerf, pierce delay, and arc voltage by thickness? Which trigger mode (2T or 4T) should the CUT45 be in for CNC use? Can Razorweld send an electronic copy of the JRWPC45LH operating manual? Answered or decided # Which manual applies to my cutter: my printed manual is the Razorweld JRWPC45LH operating manual (“CNC - CROSSFIRE COMPATIBLE”, unit “Razorweld CUT45 CNC”, built by Jasic). I couldn’t find an electronic copy online (October 2026). The online Razorcut 45 DI manual that earlier versions of this site cited is for a related but different model, so the pages now say so wherever they use it. See Sources. Residential-supply (EMC Class A) warning: dropped. It came from the Razorcut 45 DI manual, not my JRWPC45LH manual, whose safety section has no such wording. House wiring and the 230 V circuit are still a licensed electrician’s job, and I follow my manual and Langmuir’s safety page. X45 nozzle RW51206 orifice size: working answer 1.0 mm (0.040 in), per forum member mechanic416 (https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/t/21266), consistent with the torch diagram’s “20–50 amp” label. Worth confirming with Razorweld only if it matters. X45 retaining cup part number (my choice): use Langmuir’s listing, RW603505T.
